stories.title: 'CM Yogi has six days left', says Shankaracharya:Asks him to declare cow as ‘Rashtramata’
stories.summary: Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati, the Shankaracharya in Varanasi said that Yogi Adityanath still has six days to declare Gau Mata (the cow) as Rashtramata (Mother of the Nation). He said that so far no statement has come from the Chief Minister regarding the demand. According to him, several leaders from the Chief Minister’s own party have expressed support for the idea, but none have openly come forward to endorse it publicly. The Shankaracharya added that on 7 March, after reciting the Hanuman Chalisa, he will leave from Varanasi for Lucknow. There, in the presence of saints and religious leaders, he will announce the next steps of the campaign. He also said that the identities of those supporting the movement would be revealed at that time. ‘We will not deviate from our schedule’ Speaking on Thursday, the Shankaracharya said that wherever authorities stop them during the journey, they will cooperate fully with the law. He expressed hope that since the programme is a religious journey, no obstacles would be created. According to him, the group will proceed towards Lucknow according to its predetermined route and schedule. He said they would follow their path and make decisions according to religious traditions and customs. “The administration can do what it has to do, but we will not step back from our fixed schedule,” he said. Call to gather in Lucknow The Shankaracharya announced that a meeting will be held in Lucknow on 11 March focusing on the protection of cows and Sanatan Dharma. On 6 March, special worship of Bade Bhagwan Chinta Ganesh will be performed. On the same day, he will take a pledge on the birth anniversary of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, whom he described as Veer Shiromani. Later, on the evening of 7 March, he will recite the Hanuman Chalisa at the Sankat Mochan Temple in Varanasi. After this, the group will depart for Lucknow. Travelling through several districts and halting overnight at different places, they are expected to reach Lucknow on 10 March. On 11 March, coinciding with Sheetala Ashtami, a Gau Dhwaj Pratishtha (installation of the cow flag) will be organised at Kashiram Maidan in Lucknow. After this, the Shankaracharya said, a ‘Dharma Yudh’ (righteous struggle) for the protection of cows will begin, and anyone wishing to participate in the cause is welcome. Ajay Rai meets Shankaracharya Ajay Rai, the state president of the Indian National Congress in Uttar Pradesh, met the Shankaracharya at his monastery in Varanasi. During the meeting, he offered flowers at the seer’s feet, sought blessings and discussed recent developments. Rai said that when he was recently in Lucknow, the police stopped him on the way. According to him, the administration did not allow him to proceed, citing the upcoming Holi festival. He also showed Shankaracharya a letter issued by the District Magistrate, stating that it indicated the basis on which the administration was preventing people from travelling. After the meeting, the Shankaracharya said that Rai had visited him after Holi and that they had briefly discussed the Ganga campaign, although nothing particularly significant was decided. Reaction to Deputy CM’s statement A statement by Keshav Prasad Maurya, Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, has also drawn attention. Maurya had said that if the Shankaracharya came to Lucknow, he would welcome him as a devotee of Lord Ram. However, he also remarked that cows were already safe and there was no need to grant them the status of ‘State Mother’. Responding to the statement, the Shankaracharya said, 'One speaks according to one’s upbringing and values.' Congress announces support Ajay Rai said that Congress leaders and workers would stand with the Shankaracharya. He stated that they had visited the seer after Holi and that whatever instructions he gave, the entire Congress party would support him. He added that all those who consider the cow as their mother would stand united, and on 11 March, they would join the Shankaracharya in Lucknow. Background of the controversy

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:India officially condoles Khamenei's death; 6,000 UP workers fear for safety in Israel more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. India officially condoles Khamenei's death The US–Israel–Iran war has entered its sixth day. A second Iranian warship is heading towards Sri Lanka’s territorial waters on Thursday, a day after a US submarine sank an Iranian frigate, a Sri Lankan minister told parliament. 2. 6,000 UP workers fear for safety in Israel; Minister Anil Rajbhar promises govt support The widening conflict involving Israel, the United States, and Iran has now cast a long shadow over the Gulf region, impacting countries including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, and the UAE. Reports of an Indian national's death in Abu Dhabi, coupled with viral videos of stranded citizens pleading for government intervention, have sparked urgent concerns back home. 3. Shia leader Kalbe Jawad’s family stuck in Iran, 1.25 lakh Lucknow residents stranded in Gulf countries The son, sister and other family members of Maulana Kalbe Jawad, one of the biggest religious leaders of the Shia community in Lucknow, are currently stranded in Iran. Apart from them, more than 1.25 lakh people from the city are stuck in Gulf countries such as Iran, Oman, Bahrain, Muscat, Riyadh, Dubai, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah. 4. Nitish Kumar files Rajya Sabha nomination, pledges support to new Bihar govt Bihar Chief Minister and JD(U) president Nitish Kumar filed his nomination papers for the Rajya Sabha elections today. This comes after Nitish announced his decision to step down from the state’s top job and head to the Rajya Sabha. 5. Holi clash erupts in Aligarh village, man opens fire from rooftop, 13 detained A ruckus broke out over playing with colours during Holi in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh. In Padiyawal village, an argument first erupted between two groups and quickly escalated into violence. During the clash, a youth from one side climbed onto a roof and fired shots indiscriminately, injuring several people with pellets. 6. Knife attack on ex-Muslim YouTuber, CCTV shows Salim stabbed 14 times CCTV footage of the deadly attack on YouTuber Salim Wastik in Ghaziabad has surfaced, revealing how attackers Zeeshan and Gulfam brutally assaulted the ex-Muslim content creator. 7. Polling concludes for 275 seats in Nepal Voting has concluded for the Nepal General Elections. According to the primary data by the Election Commission of the country, the final voter turnout was at 60% during these elections. 8. Bhaskar team traces 'Musa Gang' members in Mauganj The Moosa Gang, whose alleged threat kept Mauganj BJP MLA Pradeep Patel away from his constituency for nearly two months, has been traced by the Bhaskar team. The details that emerged during the investigation have surprised many. 9. UP land grab racket exposed in sting Those accused of grabbing tribal land in UP themselves admitted this during a sting. The issue is being described as “land jihad”. Various methods are allegedly being used to take over tribal land. 10. Indian markets make strong comeback after Iran war impact The stock market is up on March 5, 2026. Sensex is trading at the 79,600 level with a gain of 550 points. Nifty is also up by over 170 points.

stories.title: Gorakhpur’s first six-lane flyover 95% complete:Set to open by end of March, 30-minute journey to be reduced to 5 minutes
stories.summary: Two major infrastructure projects aimed at reducing traffic congestion in Gorakhpur are now in their final stages. The six-lane flyover from Transport Nagar to Padleganj and the four-lane flyover towards Deoria Bypass are expected to be opened to the public in the last week of March. Construction work on both flyovers is progressing rapidly, with nearly 95 per cent of the work already completed. Construction work accelerated The executing agency, Setu Nigam, has significantly increased the pace of construction in recent weeks. The total length of the six-lane flyover is 2,658.187 metres. Work on constructing the pillars for the four-lane flyover towards Deoria Bypass is progressing quickly. At the same time, the construction of the approach road for the six-lane flyover towards Padleganj is also moving ahead rapidly, where soil filling work is currently underway. Mithilesh Kumar, General Manager of Setu Nigam, said that the target is to open both flyovers in March. Once operational, the projects are expected to provide relief from traffic congestion for thousands and even lakhs of commuters every day. See the latest pictures of the 6-lane flyover- Final phase of structural work The approach road towards Transport Nagar is almost complete. The space between the girders up to Rustampur has already been filled. In addition, painting work on the flyover pillars is currently underway. After the gaps between girders are fully filled, the next stage will involve the construction of the road surface. Intersection planned above flyover An intersection will also be constructed above the six-lane flyover near Deoria Bypass. Police personnel will be deployed at this point to regulate vehicle speed and ensure smooth traffic movement. The Bridge Corporation will also make arrangements for seating facilities for the deployed police personnel. Project approved in 2022, construction began in 2023 The project involves the construction of a six-lane flyover from Transport Nagar intersection via Deoria Bypass Tiraaha towards Padleganj, along with a four-lane flyover towards Deoria Bypass. The project received official approval on 18 November 2022, and construction work began in February 2023. A total of ₹429.49 crore is being spent on the two flyovers. Initially, progress remained slow due to heavy traffic movement on the Lucknow highway, which affected construction activities. Later, monitoring was increased to accelerate the work. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had earlier expressed displeasure over the slow pace of construction. Following this, officials began conducting regular reviews, and the Chief Minister himself inspected the project. Since then, the pace of work has improved considerably. Significant relief expected for commuters Once completed, the flyovers are expected to significantly reduce traffic congestion in the area. Vehicles coming from the Lucknow or Varanasi side and heading towards Taramandal will be able to directly climb onto the six-lane flyover from Transport Nagar and descend via the four-lane flyover towards Deoria Bypass. This will eliminate the need to pass through congested areas such as Transport Nagar, Mahewa, Rustampur, Nahar Road and Deoria Bypass. Similarly, vehicles travelling from Padleganj towards Lucknow or Varanasi will be able to reach Transport Nagar directly through the six-lane flyover near Deoria Bypass, significantly easing traffic movement across the city.

stories.title: Shia leader Kalbe Jawad’s family stuck in Iran:1.25 Lakh Lucknow residents stranded in Gulf countries
stories.summary: The son, sister and other family members of Maulana Kalbe Jawad, one of the biggest religious leaders of the Shia community in Lucknow, are currently stranded in Iran. Apart from them, more than 1.25 lakh people from the city are stuck in Gulf countries such as Iran, Oman, Bahrain, Muscat, Riyadh, Dubai, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah. Everyone is waiting to return home. Whenever families in Lucknow call their relatives to check on their wellbeing, sounds of bomb blasts can be heard in the background, increasing their anxiety. According to travel agency operators in the city, over 1.25 lakh people from Lucknow are currently in Gulf countries. Around 115 flights operate every week from Lucknow airport to the Gulf region, but people there are now facing difficulties due to widespread flight cancellations. Now read what people from Lucknow said about the situation in Iran Shia religious leader Maulana Kalbe Jawad said, “My sister, nephew and younger son are currently in Iran. Many of our family members live there. My son Kalbe Ahmad has been studying in Iran for a long time. The city of Qom, where he lives, has been hit by missiles. But thankfully, he is safe.” He added that his son has been in Iran for almost six years, while his nephew has been living there for around 16 years. Maulana Jawad said, ‘First we were slaves of the British, now we are of America’ Maulana Kalbe Jawad said action should be taken against Israel and America through the United Nations. He alleged that attacks on schools have killed more than 100 children. “Our government claims to oppose terrorism, but it should openly say that we follow whatever America says. Whoever America labels a terrorist, we also start calling them terrorists. We don’t have our own independent stand,” he said. He further added, “Our government has accepted Donald Trump as its master. When Trump said stop buying oil from Russia, the response was ‘Yes sir’. This shows that we have moved from British slavery to American slavery.” “We have been locked inside Trump’s trunk. Leaders should stop the hypocrisy and say clearly that earlier we were slaves of the British, and now we are slaves of America,” he said. Maulana also alleged that while peace talks were being facilitated on one side, Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was targeted in the attack, adding that they will continue to oppose such actions. Bombs fell 100 meters away Ravish Zaidi, a resident of Lucknow, works as a reporter for an Iranian state TV channel in Tehran. His father Amir Abbas Zaidi expressed concern over the worsening situation. He said his son has been living in Iran for around 17 years. “Just 15 days ago, he suffered a heart attack and underwent open heart surgery. He returned home only three days ago after being discharged from the hospital. Now suddenly the war has started, which has increased our worry,” he said. According to him, Ravish sent pictures of the place where the attack occurred. “The bombing happened about 100 metres from where my son lives. Nearly 30 bombs were dropped in that area,” he said. Narrowly escaped death last year Amir Abbas Zaidi said they tried to persuade their son to return to Lucknow, but he refused. “Whenever war begins, our anxiety increases. Last year too, when an Israeli bomb hit an Iranian building, it was being reported live. My son had moved away from that spot just 15 seconds earlier, which saved his life,” he said. “As a father, I am extremely worried. My son lives alone in Iran. His wife passed away a year ago. On June 12, 2025, when Israel attacked Iran, my wife also died here in Lucknow the same day. My son could not even attend his mother’s funeral,” he added. He said they speak on the phone regularly, but explosion sounds can often be heard during the calls. “We tried many times to convince him to leave Iran, but he does not want to come back,” he said.

stories.title: Holi clash erupts in Aligarh village:Man opens fire from rooftop, mob stones police; 13 detained
stories.summary: A ruckus broke out over playing with colours during Holi in Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh. In Padiyawal village, an argument first erupted between two groups and quickly escalated into violence. During the clash, a youth from one side climbed onto a roof and fired shots indiscriminately, injuring several people with pellets. Angered by the incident, villagers surrounded the accused’s house and began pelting stones. They attempted to break the gate and enter the premises. On receiving information, police reached the spot with a heavy force and tried to disperse the crowd after cordoning off the house. This further enraged the villagers, who started throwing stones at the police as well. An inspector sustained a head injury in the stone pelting. Additional police forces were rushed to the area and the crowd was dispersed using force. The youth who fired the shots was later arrested, while 12 others involved in the violence were also taken into custody. The area has now been turned into a virtual cantonment. The incident occurred on Wednesday in the Madrak police station area. First Image- Understand whole matter in sequence Fight broke out with neighbor during Holi celebrations According to police- Manish Varshney and Kailash live in Padiyawali village. Their houses are adjacent. On Wednesday at 3 PM during Holi celebrations, women got into an argument. They had a dispute over applying colors. The dispute escalated so much that men also started arguing with each other. Meanwhile, Kailash lost his temper. He ran and climbed onto his house's roof. He started firing. Firing from roof, neighbor and passerby got shot The pellets hit Manish's chest. He fell to the ground. Even after this Kailash didn't stop firing. During this time, a passerby named Jaswant was passing by. Pellets also hit his arm. The firing caused panic in the village. People surrounded Kailash's house and started stone pelting. Stone pelting on police, inspector's head injured Seeing people's anger, the accused locked himself inside the house. People started trying to break down the door of the house. Meanwhile, passersby informed the Madrak police station. Police reached the spot. They started moving people away from the house. During this, people started stone pelting on the police. SSI Dharampal Singh was injured in this. Police used force to drive away rioters Seeing the situation deteriorating, SSP Neeraj Jadaun was informed. Shortly after, the SSP arrived at the scene with forces from several police stations. Police used force to drive away the rioters. The accused Kailash was surrounded and taken into custody. After that, the injured were immediately admitted to a private hospital located on Agra Road. SSP says - Rioters will not be spared SSP Neeraj Jadaun said- There was an argument between two neighbors over some issue. Later the dispute took a violent turn. During this, a young man opened fire. Angry villagers started stone pelting. Police have caught the accused and brought him to the station. Currently police force is deployed in the village. Police are identifying those who pelted stones. The rioters will not be spared.

stories.title: Bhaskar team traces 'Musa Gang' members in Mauganj:MLA Pradeep Patel stayed underground for 2 months after threats from this gang
stories.summary: The Moosa Gang, whose alleged threat kept Mauganj BJP MLA Pradeep Patel away from his constituency for nearly two months, has been traced by the Bhaskar team. The details that emerged during the investigation have surprised many. Patel had disappeared from his constituency on January 3 following a dispute over a piece of land. After remaining underground for several days, he called his grandson Arjun and warned him not to step outside, claiming that the Moosa Gang posed a threat to his life. After spending several days in Bhopal, the MLA returned to his constituency on February 26 and received a grand welcome along the way. The question now being raised is: what exactly is the Moosa Gang that forced the MLA to remain away from his area for nearly 55 days? Who are its members? Is it really so dangerous that an MLA had to leave his constituency? Is the threat limited to the BJP MLA or are other leaders also afraid? What action has the police taken? To find answers to these questions and trace the so-called Moosa Gang, the Bhaskar team reached Mauganj. Here is the report… Moosa gang member found eating pakoras Two days before the MLA returned to Mauganj, on February 23, the Bhaskar team visited the town. The atmosphere appeared normal. Roads were busy as usual and people were occupied with their routine work. Stopping at a tea stall outside the Mauganj Collectorate, the reporter decided to gauge the local mood about the Moosa Gang. A few people were already present there. When asked about the gang, a man eating pakoras laughed and said, “Brother, the gang the MLA is talking about—I am also a member of that ‘Moosa Gang’.” The man identified himself as Santosh Tiwari. It was surprising that someone claiming to be part of the gang whose alleged fear kept the MLA away for 55 days was sitting there casually. Tiwari said, “There is no Moosa Gang here. This is all a creation of our MLA’s imagination. I am associated with the Sangh Parivar and naturally support the BJP. From the time of elections until before the January 3 incident, I had a very close association with MLA Pradeep Patel.” MLA says - Now if I take back my statement, it will be embarrassing Santosh said he later spoke to the MLA on the phone and asked why he was making such statements. “He told me that he wasn’t referring to me specifically and that it had just slipped out. But if he withdraws it now, it will cause embarrassment,” Santosh claimed. According to him, the root of the entire controversy is a piece of land. He said, “On January 3 there was a dispute between two parties over land near the Mauganj bypass. The matter is pending in court. MLA Pradeep Patel arrived in support of one side and sat on a protest there. That is the real reason for the dispute. I wasn’t even in the town that day.” Night of January 3rd and 6 Crore Land To verify these claims, the Bhaskar team investigated the incident that lies at the centre of the dispute. The issue concerns around 30 dismil of land near the Mauganj bypass highway, reportedly worth about ₹6 crore, over which a long-standing dispute exists between Vinod Mishra and Anil Pandey. On the evening of January 3, MLA Pradeep Patel set up a tent on the disputed land and sat on a protest in support of Vinod Mishra. By around 8 pm the atmosphere had become tense and the conflict escalated. Vinod Mishra said, “That land belongs to me. Anil Pandey’s land is behind it, but he wants to forcibly occupy mine. We had earlier reached a compromise but he tried to take possession again. So I sought help from the MLA. After checking my documents, he came to support me.” Mishra alleged that when the MLA arrived, Anil Pandey and his associates became aggressive. “They poured petrol on the MLA and moved forward to attack him. Somehow we managed to get him out, but the crowd attacked his car and its window was broken,” he said. Court stay order on land since 2008 The other side gives a completely different account. Anil Pandey said, “Vinod Mishra and the local MLA were encroaching on my land that day. I have a High Court stay order on that land. The MLA came and started dumping soil there along with Vinod.” “When I protested and asked him to listen to my side, he called the police and had me sent to jail. When my family and villagers came to know about it, they gathered there. The police then somehow took the MLA away,” Pandey claimed. Police created 'Moosa Gang' Members of the so-called Moosa Gang are seen moving freely, eating snacks and carrying out their routine work. Yet the MLA reportedly remained away from his constituency for 55 days fearing them. So how did the name “Moosa Gang” emerge? Bhaskar’s investigation found that it was mentioned for the first time in a station diary entry dated January 29, 2025, written by then Mauganj police station in-charge Sanat Dwivedi at around 1 am. According to the entry, around 10.30 pm Vipin Tripathi, Ashutosh Tiwari, Santosh Tiwari, Lallu Pandey, Ashok Chaurasia and about 40-50 others entered the police station and used abusive and insulting language, accusing the officer of corruption and favouring the other side. The officer wrote that Ashok Chaurasia and others associated with Vipin Tripathi were involved in serious crimes and that people in the locality referred to their group as the Moosa Gang. Investigation found - No such gang exists Dwivedi further wrote in the report that he lived alone with his family and feared that the group could harm or even kill him. If any incident occurred to him, he said Vipin Tripathi, Ashok Chaurasia and their associates should be held responsible. The report caused embarrassment for the police department. Senior officials ordered an inquiry and assigned it to then Additional SP Anurag Pandey. During the investigation, statements of all the people named in the report were recorded. The ASP’s final report concluded that no such gang called the Moosa Gang existed. The one named Moosa owns an auto parts shop The Bhaskar team also traced the person named Moosa, who has often been questioned by police since the controversy began. He turned out to be Ayan, who runs Ayan Auto Parts and Repairing Centre in the Mauganj market. When the team reached his shop, he was busy repairing a motorcycle. Ayan said, “Some friends sometimes used to call me Moosa. I don’t run any gang. I am an ordinary man running my shop. Since this ‘Moosa Gang’ issue came up, I have been defamed.” He added that police had taken him for questioning. “They picked me up and interrogated me,” he said. Mother said - My son is being defamed Ayan’s mother also expressed distress. She said, “My son’s name is Ayan. Friends might call him Moosa, but we are very troubled by this situation. Since the incident, police come anytime and make him sit at the station for hours.” “This affects our business and people in the neighbourhood start talking. We have a small family and run this small shop. All we want is for this harassment to stop,” she said. Congress says - MLA's well-planned conspiracy Political reactions have also been divided. Former Mauganj MLA and Congress leader Sukhendra Singh Banna called it a well-planned conspiracy. “There is no Moosa Gang here. It is a conspiracy to defame local youths. The MLA does not want to visit the constituency or listen to people’s problems,” he alleged. “If someone questions him for trying to occupy land at night, they are labelled as members of the ‘Moosa Gang’. Ironically, many of those he names were once his own associates,” Banna said. BJP leaders also dismissed MLA's claims Mauganj BJP district president Rajendra Mishra also avoided giving the issue much importance. “There is no Moosa Gang here and I face no threat. I move around freely in the district. The MLA will also return to his constituency. He is currently busy with personal work and the Assembly session in Bhopal,” Mishra said. He added that there is no atmosphere of fear in the area and the administration is functioning normally. SP said - No gang and no threat to anyone Mauganj district SP Dilip Kumar Soni gave the final official clarification. He said, “On January 3 there was a land dispute and we registered a case based on the MLA’s complaint. During the investigation we arrested the people whose names came up.” “Later we learned through social media that the MLA had spoken about threats from a ‘Moosa Gang’. We did not receive any written complaint but still verified the claim. Our inquiry found no such gang active here,” he said. Referring to the station diary entry, the SP said it only mentioned that some individuals had been referred to as the Moosa Gang by the then station in-charge, but the inquiry by the Additional SP concluded that no such gang exists.

stories.title: Holi dinner turns tragic for MBBS student:Fortuner rams scooter on overbridge; friend pleads, 'bring him back'
stories.summary: An MBBS student riding a scooter died after being hit by an uncontrolled Fortuner in Gorakhpur. The student had gone to a friend’s house to celebrate Holi and was returning to his hostel after dinner at night. The Fortuner hit his scooter head-on on the overbridge. The impact was so powerful that the student was thrown into the air and got stuck on the overbridge railing about 15 metres away, hanging face down. People from nearby areas rushed to the spot and a crowd gathered on the overbridge. Many kept making videos, but no one helped bring the student down from the railing. His body remained hanging from the railing for 30 minutes. After receiving information from passersby, police reached the spot, brought him down and took him to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. After the student’s death, his friend reached the hospital. Seeing the body, he broke down and pleaded with the doctor, saying, “Doctor sir, please bring my friend back to life.” After the accident, property dealer Golden Sahni fled with the Fortuner. Police traced and arrested him within an hour. Akash Pandey (22), a resident of Sant Kabir Nagar, was a third-year MBBS student at BRD Medical College. The incident took place around 10 pm on Wednesday at the Mohiddipur-Kauabag overbridge in the Shahpur police station area. See 3 pictures of the accident- After celebrating Holi on Wednesday, Akash Pandey went to his friend Anoop’s house in the evening. He had dinner there. Around 10 PM, he was returning to the hostel when the accident occurred at the Mohdipur-Kauabagh overbridge. According to eyewitnesses, the out-of-control Fortuner hit three to four vehicles. The other vehicles sustained minor damage, while Akash’s scooter was hit hard. His helmet came off and he suffered serious injuries, getting stuck in the railing. After the accident, people from nearby areas gathered at the spot, but no one took the student to the hospital. Meanwhile, a passerby informed the police. Police reached after about 30 minutes and brought the student down from the railing. Fellow doctors created ruckus in hospital He was taken to the medical college by ambulance, but doctors there declared him dead. After news of the student’s death spread, fellow doctors reached the hospital and created a commotion. Officials pacified them by assuring strict action. Friend broke down crying After learning about Akash Pandey’s death, his friend Anoop reached the spot and broke down in tears. He said, “He had just left my house after dinner. Doctor sir, you are a doctor, please bring my friend back to life.” People present there tried to console him. Police caught the driver after one hour Police swung into action soon after receiving information about the accident. After collecting details from people at the spot, alerts were sent to nearby police stations via wireless. Within about an hour, police tracked down the black Fortuner involved in the accident and arrested its driver.

stories.title: UP land grab racket exposed in sting:Tribal land grabbed through marriage to settle Muslims
stories.summary: A rape case was filed against me... I would have gone to jail... would have been punished. So I married the tribal woman rape victim through court marriage. Bought lands in her name. Now settling our people. Those accused of grabbing tribal land in UP themselves admitted this during a sting. The issue is being described as “land jihad”. Various methods are allegedly being used to take over tribal land. In some places, men marry tribal women and buy land in their names before settling Muslims there. In other cases, the land is in the name of tribals but is occupied by Muslims. The scale of such cases can be gauged from the fact that more than 100 cases have surfaced in Sonbhadra district alone. The administration is investigating them. Is tribal land really being grabbed in UP? What methods are being used? Who are the people involved? To find answers, the Dainik Bhaskar team conducted an investigation. Read the full exposé… For the investigation, we travelled 440 km from Lucknow to Sonbhadra. About 50 km from there, in Dudhi town and nearby villages, cases have emerged of Muslims occupying tribal land. Dudhi is the centre of this trend. Twenty years ago there were around 60 Muslim families here; now the number has risen to 202. When we studied the cases, four patterns of land grabbing emerged. Now let's understand these four patterns in sequence. Let's go to the depth of the cases related to them. The first name that came up before us was Bahadur Ali. He raped a tribal woman and, after an FIR was filed, married her in court to avoid punishment. Bahadur Ali has so far bought land in 19 places in his wife’s name and is settling his relatives there. We met Bahadur Ali with a hidden camera. While claiming innocence, he narrated how the court marriage happened. Reporter: Why did you have a second marriage with a tribal woman? Bahadur Ali: My first marriage was in 1969. Second marriage was with tribal woman Razia in 1986. My second wife's father and brother were our Harware (agricultural workers). In connection with some land, local people here made Razia file rape allegations against us. When this allegation reached the police station, I consulted with my people. Found a way that marry her in court, otherwise you won't survive. When Razia's first husband learned about this, he left her. Then we got married, she has been with us since then. Reporter: What was Razia's name when the marriage happened? Bahadur Ali: When we got married, her name was Dulariya. Since this was a nickname, we changed it to Razia. Now she writes Razia alias Dulariya. Reporter: Razia is your wife. However, the lands you purchased in her name have her father's name registered. Why is that? Bahadur Ali: The Kanhar project was ongoing. We had to be rehabilitated, we were getting a package. In 2012, we applied for her caste certificate at the tehsil. We gave the name Dulariya, but somehow the Lekhpal found out. Then he made it in the name of Razia alias Dulariya Panika daughter of Sardar. After that, we started buying land from 2013. Reporter: For all the lands purchased, your wife's name includes her father's name? Not your name? This suggests that you misused their caste? Bahadur Ali: Look, if my name was included there would be caste issues. Then the caste certificate would not be effective. Reporter: Why is there a pattern in this area where Muslim men are marrying tribal women? Buying lands? That's why you are being accused of land jihad? Bahadur Ali: There is a pattern here that even if the land is in someone's name, first settle there. Then if there is any survey, the person in whose name the land is - if they give a statement in your favor, the land would become yours. If we go to the roots of Muslims who were displaced from Sundari village and came to Baghadhu village... their lands will also be found in the name of some tribal person or another. After this when the survey happened, transfers took place. Then the people who took the land... took it with the belief that whenever a survey happens, they will get a statement from the person in whose name the land is and get it transferred to their name. Bought land in tribal wife's name and gave it to nephew Bahadur Ali had allowed a man named Enul Haq to live on his land, describing him as his nephew from Amwar village, about 3–4 km away. After the dispute surfaced, Enul left the place and returned home. We spoke to him as well. Enul said Bahadur Ali is his maternal uncle. When his uncle bought land, he gave it to him as a gift. But because of the dispute, he left the place. We then visited the house of a tribal girl Rajni (name changed) in the village. A few months ago she had filed an FIR against some influential people, alleging they threatened her to convert to Islam and marry them. The main accused in that case is Bahadur Ali, who had earlier married a tribal woman after a rape allegation. Rajni alleged that he was now trying to marry his son to her so that land could be bought in her name. Reporter: What is your case? Rajni: There is this Bahadur Ali. When I used to go to college, he would send men after me. He would say that he has 4 sons, marry one of them, convert your religion. Just like Bahadur Ali married a Hindu, he was telling me to marry his son. He said they would build a house for me, give me money. He would send men when I went to college. Out of fear, I left my studies, and because of this I missed my exams too. Reporter: When did all this happen? Rajni: It's from about 6 months ago. They kept troubling us. Wherever we went... Nasimuddin, Abdul Subhan, all of them would be there. Wherever they saw us... they would say - come sit in the car, we'll drop you. We would say if we need to go somewhere, we'll go on our own. This kept happening. When these people got released from jail, they started threatening us again. They started talking about killing us. They said - we'll kill you and dump your body. Reporter: What's the land matter? Rajni: This land belongs to Bahadur Ali. There was a land dispute... a dispute with mom. They started troubling us too. Reporter: If the path gets blocked, how will you get out? Rajni: That's why he was pressuring me for marriage. Reporter: What does your father do? Rajni: He roasts lai (snack), he is disabled. We are 4 sisters and one younger brother. They said to us - you're all girls, what can you do? Reporter: Are Bahadur Ali's people dominant? Rajni: Bahadur Ali is a land mafia. He will buy land and settle outsiders. Reporter: Does he buy in his wife's name? Rajni: Yes, he married a Hindu. He is buying and selling land in her name. He is settling people from outside. Reporter: Where are the people he has settled on his land? Rajni: Those people never lived here, they are not residents of this place. We don't have much information. Later we learned that Sirajuddin had also married a tribal woman. We went to Bagharu village, 20 km from Dudhi. Sirajuddin had two marriages—first to a Muslim woman and second to a tribal woman named Nanki. We learned that Sirajuddin had died a few years ago. Nanki was not at home when we visited. Her daughter-in-law gave little information. Documents showed that seven plots in different places are registered in Nanki’s name, all purchased by Sirajuddin. Reporter: Where has Nanki gone? Nanki's Daughter-in-law: Don't know. She has sons, she has daughters. She can go anywhere. Reporter: What is your relation to her? Nanki's Daughter-in-law: I am her daughter-in-law. Reporter: What does your husband do? Nanki's Daughter-in-law: My husband works in Gujarat. Reporter: How much land is in your mother-in-law's name? Nanki's Daughter-in-law: Now that you're here, you must already know? Reporter: Don't you get along with your mother-in-law? Nanki's Daughter-in-law: Well, there's always some friction between mother-in-law and daughter-in-law. Those who could not get land through the earlier methods adopted a fourth pattern. It does not involve direct legal violations and sometimes even benefits the tribal woman. But if authorities act, the person who paid for land in the tribal woman’s name could face losses. In Bagharu village we found such a case. Five biswa of land at Langdi Mod is registered in the name of tribal woman Kunti Jagte, but it is occupied by Ghulam Sarwar. When we spoke to him, he tried to mislead us. Reporter: Why are all these issues coming up now? Ghulam Sarwar: Now what's happening is that Muslims are settling by getting land registered based on religion. But we are not like that. Reporter: When Kunti Jagate bought the land, you and Mustakim were two witnesses. So were you in contact from before or did you come later? Ghulam Sarwar: When we found out that SC/ST land was being sold. We said you people take it, get it built. We will take it. Now I don't remember whether we were witnesses or not. Ghulam Sarwar tried to mislead us. The truth is that when the land was registered in Kunti's name, Ghulam Sarwar's signature is there as a witness. After this, we spoke to Abdul Subhan, a person from the village. He revealed the truth behind this mystery. Reporter: What is this case about Ghulam Sarwar and Kunti Jagte? Abdul Subhan: They have also registered land in the name of a Godin (Scheduled Tribe). Reporter: Are you saying that Ghulam Sarwar has registered land in someone else's name? Abdul Subhan: Yes... that's right... Reporter: How did these people come in contact with Kunti Jagte? Abdul Subhan: These people went to Chhattisgarh from Sundari village... they registered here in her name. Reporter: So this means marry a tribal woman and register the land? Abdul Subhan: This used to happen before. Those who got married earlier... they used to do it this way. But now with tribal land, these people negotiate with them. They buy land in their name by giving pressure and money. Then they settle there. This is how it's happening now. If they buy land worth 4 lakhs, they give 50 thousand to the tribal person. What's the big deal in just getting a name written? Reporter: What if the person changes their mind? Abdul Subhan: Then everything will be finished, right? Here trust is more important. How deep are the roots of Land Jihad in the village? To understand this, we spoke to Bhola, who runs a hotel outside the village. He said several people have married tribal women and are buying and selling tribal land in their names. Reporter: Are Muslims really marrying tribal women and buying lands here? Bhola: This issue that's gaining attention through Bahadur Ali. Behind this is that when a person becomes successful, their ambition grows. The ambition grew so much that wherever there was disputed land, he would try to acquire it and expand his business. Reporter: What business do they do? Bhola: Buying and selling land. When they buy disputed land, automatically there will be conflicts with tribals. Because tribals have possession. The name is someone else's, registry is somewhere else. Then when possession happens, there will definitely be disputes. Reporter: Is Bahadur Ali the only one doing this here or are others doing it too? Bhola: Many people are not visible right now. But now because of Bahadur Ali, all people will come into the limelight. Reporter: Is this pattern still continuing that Muslims are marrying tribals? Bhola: Now we don't know anyone's intentions, but they married tribals. Because inter-caste marriage is a legal right. Based on that, they got married and it becomes easier for us to buy land in their name. Now some people have taken advantage of this. That's why these people are getting caught now. We are investigating the cases that have come to light When Sonbhadra DM Badrinath Singh was asked about this matter, he refused to comment. After this, SP Abhishek Verma was contacted. He spoke about the investigation.

stories.title: 7-minute knife attack on ex-Muslim YouTuber:CCTV shows Salim stabbed 14 times; attackers carried pistols but chose brutal assault
stories.summary: CCTV footage of the deadly attack on YouTuber Salim Wastik in Ghaziabad has surfaced, revealing how attackers Zeeshan and Gulfam brutally assaulted the ex-Muslim content creator. The most shocking detail is that both brothers were carrying pistols but did not use them. Instead, they tortured Salim for nearly seven minutes, repeatedly stabbing his chest and stomach with knives and attempting to slit his throat. Salim was attacked on February 27 and suffered 14 stab wounds. He is currently admitted to a private hospital in Delhi. Doctors have performed two surgeries, but his condition remains critical. Meanwhile, police have killed both accused — Zeeshan and Gulfam — in an encounter. Read the report CCTV footage of attack on Ex-Muslim Salim Zeeshan-Gulfam entered wearing helmets At the time of the attack, Salim was alone in his office. CCTV footage shows him lying on a sofa inside the office when a bike stops outside the building. Zeeshan and Gulfam enter wearing helmets. Zeeshan walks up and stands next to Salim. Zeeshan tried to slit throat with knife, Gulfam stabbed chest and stomach Sensing danger after seeing the two men, Salim tries to react. Before he can get up, Zeeshan pulls out a surgical blade. Salim attempts to grab his hand, but Gulfam quickly launches the attack. Salim falls to the floor as Zeeshan tries to slit his throat. At the same time, Gulfam repeatedly stabs him in the chest and stomach. During the assault, Salim desperately tries to defend himself. 14 stab wounds, Zeeshan’s finger also cut Both brothers remained inside the office for about seven minutes and thirty seconds. They kept their helmets on to avoid identification. During this time, they stabbed Salim 14 times from neck to stomach. In the struggle, Zeeshan’s finger was also cut. Their clothes were soaked in blood. Salim collapsed on the floor, briefly tried to sit up again, and then fell unconscious in a pool of blood. Accused had a pistol, so why attack with knives? New revelations are emerging daily in the attack on Salim Wastik. Police have found that Zeeshan and Gulfam were carrying an Italian-made pistol when they came to attack him. They could have shot Salim instantly, but chose not to. According to police, there could be two possible reasons. First, the attackers wanted to torture and kill Salim in a brutal manner to send a strong message to YouTubers who speak against Islam. Second, the sound of gunfire could have alerted people nearby and drawn a crowd quickly, making it difficult for them to escape. Investigation underway on three angles Police are investigating the case from three different angles. First, whether someone else is the real mastermind behind the attack on Salim Wastik. Second, whether other YouTubers who speak against Islam could also be targets. Third, which organisation Zeeshan and Gulfam may have been working for. YouTube videos found in Zeeshan-Gulfam’s Google search history Police recovered details of several YouTube videos from the Google search history on the accused brothers’ mobile phones. One such video shows Salim Wastik saying that the Quran states Muslims living in a country where they should not be should leave that country. They were in contact with a Delhi Maulana In the video, Salim also reportedly says Muslims should leave India. Police believe such content provoked a section of people. Both brothers, Zeeshan and Gulfam, were residents of Khoda in Ghaziabad. However, they were reportedly in contact with a Maulana based in Delhi. Investigators believe the two attackers may have been receiving guidance from him. Both brothers went to Delhi before the attack Police have also accessed Zeeshan’s Instagram account, where he is seen delivering Islamic speeches similar to those of a Maulana. It has also emerged that both brothers travelled to Delhi shortly before the attack on Salim Wastik. The Ghaziabad Crime Branch may soon question the Maulana, as investigators are tracking funds received by Zeeshan and Gulfam, which appear to have links with him. In such circumstances, police believe more arrests could be made soon. Zeeshan–Gulfam encounter: Story in 5 points 1. Police spotted suspects, firing began According to DCP Piyush Singh, Loni SHO Nitin Chaudhary and the Rural SWAT team noticed two suspects on a bike during a late-night check. When police tried to stop them, the suspects opened fire with pistols. 2. 15 minutes of cross-firing, Zeeshan injured Police retaliated and around 25–30 rounds were fired from both sides for nearly 15 minutes. A bullet struck the SHO’s bulletproof jacket, while one of the attackers was hit and injured during the exchange. 3. Zeeshan confessed before dying The injured accused told police that he and his brother Gulfam had attacked YouTuber Salim. He was taken to a 50-bed hospital near the Nithaura underpass, where doctors declared him dead. Police recovered a .32 bore Italian-made pistol, six cartridges, eight empty shells and a Splendor bike from the spot. 4. Tip-off about Gulfam after 48 hours About 48 hours later, police received information that Gulfam was in the Indirapuram police station area. A trap was laid near the Vasundhara powerhouse to catch him. 5. Bike slips during chase, Gulfam killed in encounter Late at night, police tried to stop a bike carrying two men. Instead of stopping, they sped away under the elevated road. During the chase, their bike slipped on a dirt mound and both fell. They started firing at police, who retaliated. Gulfam was shot and injured, while his accomplice escaped in the darkness. Gulfam was taken to hospital but died during treatment. An Aadhaar card identified him as a resident of Amroha. Now let's understand the complete incident... YouTuber Salim Ahmad alias Salim Wastik (50) lives with his family in Delhi's Ashok Vihar Colony. He has another house in the Loni area of Ghaziabad. Salim runs his office from there. His son Usman said that his father was sitting alone in the office at 9 am on February 27. At that time, 2 youths wearing helmets came and attacked. As soon as they entered, they stabbed him repeatedly. Usman said - his father fell to the ground injured. Blood started flowing from his body. Meanwhile, both criminals fled. Neighbors who arrived after hearing screams informed the police. Salim was taken to a nearby hospital, from where he was referred to Delhi's Guru Teg Bahadur Hospital (GTB). His condition remains serious. Son Usman had filed a complaint with the police. In this, Ashfaq, Sonu, Shahrukh Neta, Bhati Builder and a local AIMIM leader Azgar were named. stories.title: 6,000 UP workers fear for safety in Israel:Minister Anil Rajbhar promises govt support as conflict intensifies
stories.summary: The widening conflict involving Israel, the United States, and Iran has now cast a long shadow over the Gulf region, impacting countries including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan, and the UAE. Reports of an Indian nationals death in Abu Dhabi, coupled with viral videos of stranded citizens pleading for government intervention, have sparked urgent concerns back home. In 2024, the Uttar Pradesh government, under the National Skill Development initiative, facilitated the migration of thousands of youths to Israel. Through a recruitment drive conducted by Israel's Population Immigration and Border Authority in Lucknow, approximately 6,000 workers, mostly from UP, were selected. Currently, an estimated 42,000 Indians are working across Israel. These workers are primarily engaged in critical infrastructure projects, ranging from high-rise building construction to road networks, drawn by high-paying opportunities where salaries often exceed 1 lakh per month. Geopolitical tensions and safety of Indian migrant workers The paradigm of the conflict has shifted significantly since these workers first arrived. Initially, the situation was largely localized between Israel and Hamas, and while the atmosphere was tense, the Indian community remained relatively shielded from direct harm. However, the current confrontation involves direct exchanges between Israel, supported by the U.S., and Iran. Unlike previous insurgent skirmishes, this is a state-on-state conflict involving long-range ballistic missiles and sophisticated drone technology. As the theater of war expands into the UAE and surrounding nations, the safety net for Indian laborers is thinning. To understand the reality of life under the sirens, we spoke directly with the workers on the ground. They describe a life lived between construction sites and bomb shelters, balancing the need to earn for their families back home with the instinct to flee a rapidly destabilizing region. 16 people from one village, say - all are safe 16 people from Sahabpurwa Mauza of Shahnawazpur village in Bahraich have gone to Israel. These people are currently in Katsarin. This is about 250 kilometers away from Israel's capital Jerusalem. Abhinav Nishad works here as an engineer. The rest of the people work as laborers. We asked Abhinav Nishad when did you go to Israel and what is the current situation? Abhinav said - I have been here for more than 5 years. The rest of the people came in 2024. Currently, we live near the Lebanon-Syria border. There is no problem in this area regarding the ongoing fight with Iran. But when the siren sounds occasionally, we all become alert. We immediately go to the bunker. Now bunkers are being built with every flat Abhinav explains - Every part of Israel is full of danger. Whether you go to any building, park, or stay on the road, you will find underground bunkers everywhere. Now the situation has become such that bunkers are being built with every flat. The wall of the bunker is 2.5 to 3 feet thick. All construction here is done with RCC, bricks are not used anywhere in house construction. Last year when there was fighting from Gaza, missiles could be seen continuously going through the sky here. At that time, such a situation would arise every day that we had to go to the bunker. Currently, there are reports of attacks near Tel Aviv and Jerusalem. Where we are, the situation is normal here. There was one blast, but no danger Ramachal Nishad from Bahraich is also working in Katsrin. He went to Israel under the UP government scheme. Speaking about the current situation, he says - ever since the war started, we have been feeling scared. Because Iran is continuously attacking in this war. I see in the news daily that attacks are happening somewhere in Dubai or Bahrain. 3 days ago, a missile also fell, we all saw that video. Everyone has been scared since then. Ramachal says - We are not as scared as our family members back home. They make video calls intermittently to check on the situation around. I show them the bunker and explain that there is no situation of attack here yet. The security system is high-tech. Only then are they able to stay at ease. Regarding coming back, Ramachal says - We have no intention of returning right now. There is no problem of any kind here. PM Narendra Modi had visited here recently. He met with some people. He also discussed our security. The officials here informed that everyone is fine. UP government is continuously monitoring Currently, more than 42 thousand citizens of the country are living in Israel. This includes 6004 construction workers from UP. Most of them have gone within the last 2 years. UP's Labor Minister Anil Rajbhar says on this entire matter - UP government is committed to the safety of all workers. We are in constant touch with the National Skill Development Corporation and the embassy there. So far no problems of any kind have come to light. The Indian Embassy is located in Tel Aviv, Israel. Officials have issued helpline numbers. These numbers are +972-54-7520711, +972-54-2428378. Additionally, PIBA has also issued the number 1-700-707-889. This is being operated by the Center for International Migration and Integration

stories.title: Lucknow celebrates India’s T20 World Cup victory on streets:Fans gather with tricolours, burst firecrackers and dance in Hazratganj
stories.summary: Celebrations have broken out across Lucknow following India’s victory in the T20 World Cup. People have gathered at major intersections carrying the national tricolour and distributing sweets. Firecrackers are being burst and coloured powder is being thrown in the air. Amid the celebrations, the Hazratganj area has become completely congested. Even before the match ended, people had begun dancing to ‘bhangra’ in areas such as Kapurthala and Hazratganj. CM Yogi Adityanath also posted on X and congratulated the Indian Cricket Team Large screens installed across the city In several parts of the city, arrangements had been made for residents to watch the match together. Large screens and projectors were installed at multiple locations. LED screens were set up in markets, while parks hosted tented viewing areas where people watched the match on projectors. Big screens were placed at Rajajipuram, Madiyanv and Kapurthala intersections. In Gomti Nagar’s Vinamra Khand park, residents gathered to watch the match collectively. In the Ismailganj Second Ward area, the World Cup final was screened on a large display at Dayal Park alongside a Holi Milan celebration. Match screened at social gatherings At Annapurna Ground in Nigohan, a tilak ceremony also featured an LED screen where guests and invitees watched the match together. Earlier in the day, a marathon in support of Team India was organised at the 1090 intersection by the Lucknow Super Giants franchise. Later, a havan was performed in Gomti Nagar with prayers for India’s victory. Due to the large number of fans gathering in central areas, the police are struggling to manage traffic. The presence of cricket supporters has caused traffic to come to a halt in Hazratganj. See 7 pictures of the celebration-

stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav once again raised the issue of Keshav Maurya's helicopter's emergency landing. He said- The most worn-out and bad helicopter was given to the Deputy CM. I heard that it caught fire. It was filled with smoke. Our Deputy CM's life was saved. According to protocol, the Deputy CM should get a new helicopter. Why wasn't he given the new one? He wasn't given it because he is PDA. Akhilesh Yadav reached the home of social worker Mewalal in Jankipuram, Lucknow, on Sunday. Mewalal's son is getting married this evening. It was here that when journalists asked a question related to the President's protocol in Bengal, Akhilesh Yadav targeted the BJP. He said- BJP will find fault with anything, one should be very careful with them. One should be very careful with conspiracies and plots. How much do they follow protocol? They should tell how much protocol they follow? How much respect do they give to others? What Akhilesh saidin 3 points What did the SP chief say yesterday? Akhilesh Yadav had said on Saturday that Keshav Maurya should remain healthy. Such an incident should not happen to anyone. Because, it's a machine and we all fly in that machine. We all travel. The machine should always be good.

Tehran hints at consensus on next Supreme Leader, Israel threatens Khamenei’s successor Today marks the ninth day of the US-Israel and Iran conflict. Members of Iran’s Assembly of Experts have hinted that a consensus may have been reached on who will succeed the late Ali Khamenei as the country’s next supreme leader. 2. Mayawati targets Mamata over President Murmu visit controversy: Calls protocol breach unfortunate Mayawati on Sunday criticised the alleged protocol breach during the recent West Bengal visit of Droupadi Murmu and said constitutional posts should never be politicised. 3. Who is the Maulana behind provocative remarks about Yogi’s mother?: Studied from Deoband Bihar's Maulana Abdullah Salim Chaturvedi made objectionable and inflammatory statements about CM Yogi Adityanath's mother. This angered BJP workers and Yogi fans. 6. Brick kiln worker’s son becomes IAS: Vimal Kumar from Raebareli secures 107th rank in UPSC Ramdev’s son Vimal Kumar, who worked at a brick kiln in Raebareli, has become an IAS officer, securing 107th rank in UPSC. To celebrate his success, Vimal led a 7-kilometre procession with a convoy. 7. Over 52,000 Indians return from Gulf amid tensions in west Asia India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Saturday that over 52,000 Indians returned safely from Gulf countries between March 1 and 7, 2026, amid tensions in West Asia. 8. LKG student kidnapped in front of grandfather in Prayagraj: 2 criminals flee after dragging child into car On Saturday, an LKG student was kidnapped in broad daylight in Prayagraj. The student was returning home from school. As soon as he got out of the school van, two criminals pulled him into a car and fled. 9. Varanasi woman turns cow dung into livelihood for thousands: Rita Tiwari trains nearly 6,000 women When intentions are as strong as steel, and the goal is social welfare, even seemingly ordinary resources become a means of extraordinary change. 50-year-old Rita Tiwari, a resident of Tarna Yamuna Nagar Colony in Shivpur police station area of Varanasi district, Uttar Pradesh, has proven this to be true. 10. Anil Ambani booked in new ₹1,085-crore fraud case The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has registered a new fraud case against former Reliance Communications (RCom) director Anil Ambani and others.

stories.title: CM Yogi attends 'Pink Rozgar Mahakumbh' event in Lucknow:Announces free scooties for girl students, employment will be given to 5,000 women
stories.summary: During the ‘Pink Rozgar Mahakumbh’ event in Lucknow, Minister Pratibha Shukla sang a song on stage. Listening to the performance, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath responded with humour and said that when Pratibha Shukla was singing, he was thinking it was good that she was singing now, otherwise Lata Mangeshkar might have taken retirement. After remarking, Yogi burst into laughter and said that the title of Swar Samragni should actually have been given to her. He then added that it was still a good effort. He said that when someone overcomes hesitation and speaks or performs publicly, it reflects their confidence. Women’s Day programme at IGP In fact, Yogi was speaking at a programme organised on the occasion of Women’s Day at IGP. During the event, he distributed cheques to girls under the Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana. He also interacted warmly with beneficiaries. He affectionately handed a teddy bear to a young girl who had accompanied one of the beneficiaries and also gave her chocolates. The Chief Minister spoke with young women present at the programme and encouraged one of them by saying, ‘Study well and become successful.’ Announcement of free scooties for students Addressing the gathering, the Chief Minister announced that the government would soon provide free scooties to girl students. The benefit will be given to students in the final year of graduation and post-graduation. He said that daughters would no longer have to depend on anyone, and the government would support them in both education and employment. Employment and initiatives under Pink Mahakumbh 2026 Under Pink Mahakumbh 2026, there is a plan to provide employment opportunities to 5,000 women. The event will also witness the launch of the Sangam portal mobile application, distribution of appointment letters to 94 newly appointed mukhya sevikas, and the presentation of Nari Shakti Awards. Additionally, Anganwadi workers will receive ₹3,849 lakh directly in their bank accounts through the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system. See 4 pictures-

stories.title: Mayawati targets Mamata over President Murmu visit controversy:Calls protocol breach unfortunate; asks parties to respect constitutional posts
stories.summary: Mayawati on Sunday criticised the alleged protocol breach during the recent West Bengal visit of Droupadi Murmu and said constitutional posts should never be politicised. In a post on X, the BSP supremo said everyone should respect the dignity and protocol attached to the office of the President as per the ideals of the Indian Constitution. She said the current President is not only a woman but also belongs to the tribal community, and the events during her recent visit to West Bengal were “extremely unfortunate”. Mayawati’s remarks came amid a political controversy over the absence of senior state representatives during Murmu’s visit to North Bengal. Mayawati also raises issue of Lok Sabha Speaker’s dignity Mayawati also criticised the opposition’s behaviour in Parliament towards the Om Birla. She said the politicisation of the Speaker’s position in Parliament in recent times was not appropriate and urged all parties to rise above political differences and maintain the dignity of constitutional posts. The BSP chief also appealed for the smooth functioning of Parliament in the interest of the country and public welfare. The second phase of the Budget Session of Parliament will begin on March 9. What happened during President Murmu’s West Bengal visit? President Murmu had arrived in North Bengal near Siliguri on March 7 to attend the 9th International Santhal Conference. The venue of the event was reportedly changed at the last moment from Bidhannagar to Gosaipur. The size of the venue was also smaller, due to which many members of the tribal community could not attend the programme. Another issue that sparked controversy was the absence of senior leaders from the state government to receive the President. Traditionally, the Chief Minister of a state welcomes the President during official visits. In the Chief Minister’s absence, the senior-most minister usually receives the President. However, neither West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee nor any state minister was present to receive Murmu. During the programme, the President expressed displeasure over the matter. She said that as per protocol, the Chief Minister or a minister from the state government should have been present to receive her. Murmu added that she personally had no objection but said such traditions should be followed to maintain dignity and protocol. PM Modi says President’s office is above politics Narendra Modi also commented on the controversy on X. He said people who believe in strengthening democracy and the tribal community were saddened by the incident. Modi added that the office of the President is above politics and its dignity should always be maintained. He also expressed hope that the West Bengal government and the Trinamool Congress would reflect on the matter. Mamata Banerjee hits back at criticism Responding to the controversy, Mamata Banerjee said criticism of West Bengal was politically motivated. She said before commenting on West Bengal, the President should first look at the situation in states ruled by the BJP. Speaking at a protest site in Kolkata, Banerjee alleged that the BJP was trying to defame West Bengal by using President Murmu. She also said the information given to the President about the absence of state representatives at the event was incorrect.

stories.title: Father kills 2 children, hangs himself:In Maharajganj he wrote on wall wife and her lover responsible; woman works in armed forces
stories.summary: In Maharajganj, the husband of a female Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel killed his innocent son and daughter before committing suicide. He hung both children from the window using a rope. Then he committed suicide by hanging himself from the roof hook. Before dying, the husband wrote a suicide note on the room wall - 'The cause of our death is my wife and her lover Sonu Gautam. Even while living with me, she talks to Sonu. I cannot separate the children from myself.' The incident occurred at 7 AM on Sunday. When the husband killed the children, they screamed. Hearing this, tenants living on the lower floor became suspicious. They called out but got no response. They came up to check. They knocked on the door but it didn't open. Then they called the female personnel. She was on duty at that time. The female personnel came home after a while. She knocked on the door, but it didn't open. After breaking down the door, everyone was shocked to see inside. The bodies of the 4-year-old son and 3-year-old daughter were hanging by the window. Meanwhile, the husband's body was hanging in the room. Police and SSB jawans also reached the spot. Due to duty at the Nepal border in Nautanwa, the female jawan lived on rent with her family in the Gandhi Nagar area. Her husband stayed at home and did not do any work. The family originally belongs to Saidpur in Ghazipur. See three pictures Tenant heard screaming Vandana Bharti (35) is posted in the fourth class at the 66th Battalion SSB in Nautanwa. She married Amresh (40) in 2019. She has been working since before marriage. She came here a year ago, before that she was posted in Jharkhand. Vandana lived on the first floor of a rented house here with her husband, son Amarendra Kumar (4) and daughter Kanchan (3). On Saturday evening, Vandana went on duty. Then she came early Sunday morning and after finishing her work, went back on duty. Around 7 am, the tenant living downstairs in the house heard screaming. When he went upstairs, Vandana's room gate was locked from inside. After this, he called Vandana. Children found hanging from window and husband from fan hook Vandana left her duty and came to the room. When she broke down the door and entered, she was shocked by the scene. She fainted upon seeing the bodies of her son, daughter and husband. Vandana's entire family was gone. When she regained consciousness after a while, she lay on the floor crying and flailing her arms and legs. She fainted again while crying and holding onto the bodies of the innocents. Amaresh wrote a suicide note on the wall- Even while staying with me, Vandana calls Sonu. She says you can't do anything to me. I can't keep my children away. The cause of our death is my wife Vandana Kumari (SSB) and her lover Sonu Gautam, Vandana's father Ram Avatar, mother Chanda Devi, brother Naveen Kumar, his wife Sunita Devi and Amarnath. These people call my wife to their home for money. Wife gives 5000 rupees every month. Her lover Sonu Gautam also takes this money. Because of Sonu, the entire family is destroyed today. Before suicide, Amrish made a video and sent it to his brother-in-law, read what he said? My wife should not touch my body, she has ruined me I, Amrish Thakur, am issuing this statement in full consciousness. The cause of our death is none other than my wife and her family members. My wife is Vandana Kumari (SSB 66th Battalion). My wife often says that she will take me to the camp and have me beaten with sticks and will also have my family members picked up. She used to say give me a divorce, or I will ruin you. We have two children, so how could I divorce and leave them? She would insult me by calling me unemployed. If I was unemployed, why did she marry me? Why didn't she see all this before marriage? Today she has defamed and ruined me to such an extent that I am not in a position to do anything. I want to tell everyone that any unemployed person should think very carefully before marrying a working woman. About 7 months ago, since July, my wife was talking to a person named Sonu Gautam. She said she would only marry him. They had a relationship. I hid many of her mistakes, didn't tell anyone anything. Who can a man share his troubles with? Even the laws in the world are mostly made in favor of women. No one listens to men's side. I am not able to tell my family about my troubles. It causes a lot of pain. Now I am completely helpless. My last wish is that after my death my wife should not touch my body. If possible, my body should be handed over to my family members. Family dispute caused the incident ASP Siddharth said- Before dying, Amaresh had made a video and sent it to his brother-in-law too. Family dispute is being cited as the reason for the incident. Further action will be taken after the post-mortem report comes.

stories.title: Ballia SDM bitten by pet dog seeks 8-day leave:Sends application with thumb impression to DM; travels to Delhi for treatment
stories.summary: In Ballia, SDM Alok Pratap Singh was bitten by a pet dog. He requested 8 days of leave from the DM. He wrote in the application - The dog bit me on both hands, causing deep wounds. I received treatment from a local doctor, but the bleeding from the wounds is not stopping. He further wrote - I am unable to do any of my work. Doctors have advised me to consult a good hospital and a specialist doctor. Therefore, I request permission for leave from March 6th to March 13th. Following this, the DM granted him 8 days of leave. Thumbprint on the application Alok Pratap Singh is the SDM in Bairia Tehsil. He is a 2023 batch PCS (Provincial Civil Service) officer. On March 5, he wrote an application to the DM asking for leave. He put a thumbprint on the letter instead of a signature. DM Mangala Prasad Singh said- A leave application has been submitted. The SDM was bitten by a dog on his hand. He is unable to write due to a plaster cast on his hand. 'I have come to Delhi for treatment' Dainik Bhaskar spoke to SDM Alok Pratap. He said, I have come to Delhi for treatment. My mother and father arrived on the night of March 2nd. My pet dog was excited to meet them. On March 3rd, we were all sitting in the lawn in the morning, drinking tea. My pet dog was barking. I was bringing him towards my parents, holding his leash. Meanwhile, he bit one of my hands with his jaws. To get free, I tried to pull him away with my other hand. This injured both my hands. A staff member present there poured water on the dog from a bottle, and only then did he let go of me. Currently, I am on medical leave. Accused of getting domestic work done Alok Pratap Singh took charge as Deputy Collector in Ballia on February 12, 2024. In January 2026, he was accused by a home guard of being removed from duty, made to do domestic work, and misbehaving. Additionally, a former MLA had raised questions about him regarding the active presence of brokers in the tehsil.

stories.title: Brother-in-law kills sister-in-law in Etawah:Eloped and married; man later informs police about body at home
stories.summary: A 35-year-old brother-in-law killed his 18-year-old sister-in-law in Etawah. 4 days ago, on Holi, he had eloped with his sister-in-law to Delhi. There, they got married in a temple. On Saturday morning, he reached home from Delhi. At night, he argued with his sister-in-law, Sunaina. In anger, he killed her by hitting her with bricks. After the incident, he went to the police station with the blood-stained brick. He told the police officers, "I have committed murder. The body is lying at home. Pick it up." The accused Vijay Kushwaha works as a contract mechanic in the Delhi Jal Board. 5 years ago, he had a love marriage with Nisha Kathariya. At that time, too, they had eloped to get married. Both families had later accepted their relationship. Vijay and Nisha also have a 3-year-old son. 2 months ago, Vijay had a dispute with Nisha. Since then, Nisha had been living at her parents' home. Meanwhile, Vijay got into an affair with Nisha's cousin, Sunaina. The entire incident took place in the Karanpura area of Etawah Kotwali. When police reached the house, blood was scattered in the room After accused Vijay surrendered, the police reached his house. The body was lying on the floor in the room. There was blood scattered everywhere. Police informed Sunaina's family. The body was sent for a post-mortem. Accused Vijay Kushwah's parents live with him in Delhi. Due to having a house and land in the village, he used to come here often. Deceased Sunaina's father, Raghuraj, said, 'Vijay used to visit our house daily'. On March 4, Vijay lured and eloped with our daughter. He took her to Delhi and got married there. We spoke to her on the phone and asked her to come home. On Saturday evening, daughter Sunaina called her mother. She said, 'Mom, we will come home, please don't beat us'. Around 3 AM, we got a call from the police station to come to the district hospital. When we reached there, we saw our daughter lying on a stretcher in the hospital. Vijay had killed her. Vijay is much older than my daughter. Police told us that injury marks were found on her body and rope marks on her neck. Sunaina's brother Shivam said - We had told mom many times not to let Vijay come to the house. But no one listened to us. He came one day before Holi. On the day of Holi, he ran away with my sister. They got married in a temple in Delhi and also sent photos and videos. Met sister-in-law while going to convince wife Shivam said - Vijay's character is not good. 5 years ago, he had also eloped and married our aunt's daughter, Nisha. There has been discord between Vijay and Nisha for the last two months. Vijay often used to come to his in-laws' house in Barra village of Baidpura to convince his wife, Nisha. That's where he met Sunaina. Sunaina's house was also in the same village. Gradually, an affair started between the two. After this, Vijay started meeting Sunaina. Kidnapping case was registered Shivam said - When Vijay took Sunaina on March 4, we filed a kidnapping case against him at the Saifai police station. Station House Officer Inspector Yashwant Singh said that the accused himself informed the police about the murder. After this, he was taken into custody. The matter is being investigated. No written complaint has been received from the family yet. Action will be taken as soon as it is received.
