stories.title: Adulterated mustard oil worth ₹6 cr seized in UP:38 firms get notice; doctor warns of heart diseases
stories.summary: Large-scale adulteration has been found in edible oil being sold in Uttar Pradesh. Low-quality oils are being mixed with mustard oil, while chemicals are being added to create colour and foam before the product is sold in the market. The revelations came during action taken by the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA). The investigation led to several shocking findings. FIRs have been registered in Unnao and Muzaffarnagar, while notices have been issued to 38 oil companies and firms. Why was this action taken? What kind of adulteration or shortcomings were found? How many firms were inspected during the campaign? How much oil was seized and how many FIRs were filed? Read this report to know more… Teams from other districts conducted investigation Joint Food Commissioner Harishankar Singh told Dainik Bhaskar that a large-scale campaign was carried out on the instructions of Commissioner Roshan Jacob. For the drive, teams from one district were sent to inspect units in other districts. FSDA teams reached 66 units in total, of which eight were found closed. Action was taken at 58 units, from where 231 samples were collected. About 4.32 lakh litres of oil were seized, with an estimated value of ₹6.5 crore. Name of mustard, selling rice bran oil Harishankar Singh said mustard oil is expensive, and companies were selling rice bran oil (extracted from rice husk) for higher profits. The information printed on the bottle labels was also concealed. Similarly, palm oil was being sold as rice bran oil. In Unnao and Muzaffarnagar, colour and essence were being used in edible oil. Licences in both places have been suspended and FIRs registered against the company owners at local police stations. Continuous consumption of adulterated mustard oil can lead to fat accumulation in heart muscles, increasing the risk of heart attack. Deficiencies found in 38 out of 58 units inspected Harishankar Singh said that of the 58 units inspected by the FSDA, irregularities were found in 38 units. Notices have been issued to these units asking them to rectify the shortcomings. If they fail to comply, their licences will be suspended. Cases found during the inspection included mixing cheaper palm oil or rice bran oil and selling it under the label of mustard or soybean oil. Other practices included adding chemical colours, artificial flavours and argemone oil to make the oil appear pure, relabelling expired or contaminated oil with new stickers before selling it in the market, and using fake branding to sell substandard oil at higher prices. The raids were conducted at 58 units between February 20 and 28. FIRs filed in these cases 11,750 liters of mustard oil was seized from Kavya Trading Company in Budhana, Muzaffarnagar and FIR was registered. Similarly, in Bangarmau of Unnao, 3,855 liters of oil was seized and operations were shut down. FIR has also been registered after finding adulteration on a large scale. Expired mustard oil caught in Gorakhpur In Gorakhpur’s Sahjanwa area, raids were conducted at the factory and warehouse of GRL Edible Private Limited, where oil worth ₹24 lakh was seized. This included expired mustard oil worth ₹10 lakh, whose old expiry date had been replaced with a new sticker showing the year 2026. The sale of Radha Rani brand rice bran refined oil worth ₹14 lakh was also stopped. Investigators found that cheap palm oil imported from Nepal at ₹80 per litre was being mixed with chemicals and sold as mustard oil for ₹160 per litre. Health risks from consuming adulterated oil To understand the health impact of adulterated oil, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to cardiologist Dr Rohit Gupta of Gorakhpur District Hospital. He said when cheaper oils such as rice bran oil, palm oil or argemone oil and chemicals are mixed with mustard oil, it becomes extremely dangerous. Several medical studies have also shown that adulterated mustard oil can cause serious health problems. It increases the risk of heart disease, liver damage and dropsy. Harmful substances such as argemone oil present in adulterated oil can severely affect the human body.

stories.title: 8 deaths on Holi in Lucknow:248 patients reach KGMU Trauma Centre, around 800 treated in emergency within 24 hours
stories.summary: More than 800 people were injured during Holi celebrations in Lucknow. Most of the cases were linked to road accidents, especially those caused by drunk driving. Many people were taken to hospitals across the city for treatment. In the last 24 hours alone, 248 injured people reached the Trauma Centre of KGMU for treatment. Doctors admitted several patients and provided medical care. Around 72 people were injured due to high-speed accidents during the Holi celebrations. Some patients also suffered health problems because of chemical colours and suspected poisoning. According to hospital sources, two critically ill patients died during treatment. One patient is still on a ventilator in critical condition. Apart from this, six people had already died before they could reach the hospital. Government hospitals treated more than 300 injured people, while around 100 patients received treatment in private hospitals. So many patients reached the Trauma Center Dr. Premraj, Chief Medical Superintendent of the Trauma Center located at KGMU, stated that 248 people came for treatment, and among them, 75 to 80 people were injured in road accidents. Of these, about 40 people were injured in road accidents due to alcohol consumption. 365 patients reached Balrampur Dr. Himanshu Chaturvedi, CMS of Balrampur Hospital, informed that 365 patients arrived at the emergency OPD. Out of these, 51 patients needed to be admitted. The rest were sent home after providing primary treatment. 21 injured people needed stitches. He informed that 73 people came to get rabies injections during Holi. Out of these, 70 percent were old patients and 30 percent were new patients. 487 patients came to Lokbandhu Dr. Ajay Shankar Tripathi, Medical Superintendent of Lokbandhu Rajnarayan Hospital, informed that 487 patients came to the emergency in 24 hours. Out of these, 60 people were injured in road accidents during Holi. 37 patients were admitted and provided treatment. The remaining patients were sent home after primary treatment. 70 patients came to Civil Hospital. Out of these, 17 patients have been admitted and are being provided treatment. 246 patients reached Lohia 246 patients arrived at the emergency OPD of Lohia Institute. Treatment was provided to 75 patients in the surgery department. Two serious patients were admitted to the ICU. Three patients were admitted. The remaining patients were discharged after primary treatment. 27 injured patients arrived in the orthopedics department. While 144 patients arrived in the emergency medicine department. Two serious patients are admitted in critical condition. A total of 30 patients have been admitted. 74 Patients headed to SGPGI 74 injured patients arrived at SGPGI's Apex Trauma Center. Of these, more than 20 patients needed to be admitted. The remaining patients were discharged after treatment. More than 75 patients were admitted and provided treatment at Rani Laxmibai, Thakurganj Joint Hospital, Mahanagar Bhaurao Deoras, and Ram Sagar Mishra Hospital located in BKT Sadhamau. Meanwhile, more than 100 patients were admitted to private hospitals in the city. Color reaction led to hospitalization Many patients had also arrived with problems like eye irritation, etc., due to the side effects of colors, and were discharged after immediate treatment. According to the data released by Lohia Institute, around 52 patients fell victim to the revelry of Holi and reached the emergency for treatment.

stories.title: 'I am from staff let me go' says drunk SI:Crowd surrounds him in Shahjahanpur after bike collision; constables carry him away
stories.summary: In Shahjahanpur, a sub-inspector, drunk and driving a car, hit a bike. The young man riding the bike was injured. After the accident, the crowd surrounded the sub-inspector's car. When asked to get out, the sub-inspector said he was "staff." Hearing this, people got agitated and started creating a ruckus. Meanwhile, people called the police. When two constables arrived at the scene and started taking the drunk sub-inspector away from the clutches of the crowd, the sub-inspector began to stumble. During this, the crowd also tried to free the sub-inspector by pushing and shoving. Seeing the situation worsen, both constables carried the sub-inspector to the police station. People made a video of this entire incident. The accident occurred in the Banda police station area. The injured bike rider has been admitted to the hospital. His two daughters were also on the bike, who narrowly escaped. See 2 pictures of the commotion Now know the full story Sunil, a resident of Utra Tikri, was going to Khutar on his bike with his two daughters, Parul and Saloni, on Thursday. Around 1 PM, near the main intersection of Banda, his bike was hit by a Swift car (UP14 FC 3337). Sunil was injured in this accident. However, his daughters narrowly escaped. After the accident, people surrounded the car. A police cap was kept on the dashboard of the car. Upon opening the door, it was found that the driver was Sub-Inspector Jogesh Sharma, posted at Banda police station. He was going to perform his duty in his area by car. People did not let the sub-inspector close the car door When people asked the sub-inspector to come out, he folded his hands and said, "I am staff, let me go." At this, people got agitated. They started saying, "If you are staff, does that mean you can hit anyone?" Hearing this, the sub-inspector started closing the car door, but people did not let him close it. Despite much effort, the sub-inspector did not get out of the car. Meanwhile, due to the commotion of the crowd, a traffic jam started on the road. After this, someone informed the police about the incident. Following this, two constables, who were playing Holi at the police station, arrived at the scene. They somehow pulled the sub-inspector out of the car and started taking him with them. At this, people began pushing and shoving to grab the sub-inspector. However, the policemen did not let go of the sub-inspector. Sub-inspector seen stumbling In the video, the sub-inspector is seen walking unsteadily. When he couldn't walk on his own feet, both policemen carried the sub-inspector on their shoulders and took him to the police station on their bike. People alleged that Sub-inspector Jogesh was heavily intoxicated. Before hitting the bike, he had also hit the divider. Banda police station in-charge said- Sub-inspector Jogesh Sharma was going in his area. There was a minor collision, due to which three people on the bike fell. One youth sustained minor injuries. The sub-inspector also sustained minor injuries. Perhaps for this reason, he was unable to walk properly.

stories.summary: For tribal and Dalit families stranded on a landmass within the vast Indravati reservoir in Odisha’s Kalahandi district, life remains in limbo. stories.title: 70% of Samajwadi Party’s district presidents are Muslim or Yadav:Why does Akhilesh trust more on these communities despite the PDA slogan?
stories.summary: After losing the race for power in Uttar Pradesh in 2022, the Samajwadi Party (SP) started raising the slogan of PDA, which stands for Pichda, Dalit and Muslim. The party used this slogan to strengthen its social coalition. The strategy showed results in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Out of 80 seats in Uttar Pradesh, the SP won 37 seats. Its ally Congress, which contested the election in alliance with the party, also managed to win 6 seats. After this success, many believed that the SP would reflect the PDA formula within its own organisation and bring a new political approach. It was expected that leaders from backward classes, Dalits and Muslims would get wider representation in the party structure. However, the current organisational structure tells a different story. Even today, about 70 per cent of the party’s 97 district and metropolitan presidents belong to the Yadav and Muslim communities, often referred to as the M-Y combination. This has raised questions about whether the PDA slogan has actually been implemented within the party organisation. Why is SP unable to trust beyond the M-Y equation in its organisation? What does it mean not to give a single Thakur a place in the organisation? How many upper castes has SP finally trusted? Read this report 2 posts vacant out of 97 District/Metropolitan Presidents of SP SP has a total of 97 District Presidents and Metropolitan Presidents across 18 divisions of the state. In Prayagraj, the SP has appointed three presidents for Gangapar, Yamunapar, and Prayagraj city. Among them, 2 are Muslim and one is Yadav. Additionally, District Presidents and City or Metropolitan Presidents have been appointed in Gorakhpur, Ayodhya, Lucknow, Bareilly, Moradabad, Ramnagar, Shahjahanpur, Agra, Firozabad, Mathura, Aligarh, Kanpur, Farrukhabad, Jhansi, Varanasi, Meerut, Ghaziabad, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Saharanpur, and Muzaffarnagar. Out of 97 posts, the positions for Bijnor and Rampur city are currently vacant. The last major reshuffle among SP's District Presidents took place on April 7, 2023. At that time, the state leadership was in the hands of Naresh Uttam Patel. In the 2024 Lok Sabha, when SP made Naresh Uttam Patel its Lok Sabha candidate, it handed over the reins to Shyam Lal Pal, a highly backward face from the OBC community. One reason for this was also Vishwanath Pal, who was made from this community by BSP. SP feared that due to Vishwanath Pal, the Pal (Gaderia community) might distance themselves from SP. Although, it's been almost 2 years since Shyam Lal Pal became president, but so far he has been able to make only a few changes. There was a possibility of large-scale reshuffling of district presidents before the assembly elections. However, due to SIR, this is also said to be pending. 44 percent Yadavs among SP District Presidents Even though the Yadav population in the state is estimated to be between 8-9 percent, the SP has taken great care of this core vote bank in its organization. Out of the current 95 district presidents, 44 percent, meaning 42, are Yadavs. Muslims are in second place. There are Muslim district presidents in 24 places. Even though the Dalit population in the state might be 20-21 percent, only 3 Dalits have been made district presidents in the SP. During Mulayam Singh's time, Thakurs used to dominate the SP. However, currently there is not a single Thakur district president or city president. Out of 95 district presidents, only 7 positions have been given to people from the general category. Among these, there are 2 Brahmins, 2 Baniyas, and 1 each Tyagi and Bengali Kayastha. BSP state president Vishwanath Pal, while taunting SP's PDA slogan, says - the conduct, character and face of any party are visible when it is in power. SP had achieved success in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections with the PDA slogan. Akhilesh Yadav himself reached the Lok Sabha by becoming an MP from an MLA. Before this, he was the leader of the opposition in the UP Assembly. He had the opportunity then to give this post to a PDA member, but he did not. The PDA slogan is being used only to get votes. Now their PDA's true colors have been exposed. Now people are looking towards BSP with hope. In 2027, under the leadership of BSP, Behan Mayawati will become the Chief Minister for the 5th time. SP relies on Muslims in the west, and Yadavs in the east SP has shown the most reliance on Muslims in Western UP. In Purvanchal, Yadavs are the most numerous district presidents. Some divisions are such where only the M-Y combination is seen. These divisions include Chitrakoot, Azamgarh, Basti, and Lucknow. However, the population of both in the state is only 27 percent. If we talk about the most balanced divisions according to the caste equation, they are the Agra and Kanpur divisions. In the Agra division, there are 7 district presidents, and posts for city and metropolitan presidents. Among these are 2 Yadav, 2 Muslim, 1 Baniya, 1 Kushwaha, and 1 Shakya district presidents. Similarly, among the 8 district presidents of Kanpur division, there are 2 each of Yadav, Muslim, and Brahmin, and 1 each of Shakya and Dalit. BJP spokesperson Rakesh Tripathi, taking a dig, says- SP's PDA model was just a facade. Outside the family, they will not give any major responsibility to anyone. Similarly, in the organization too, they don't look beyond the M-Y equation. SP spokesperson Udayveer Singh, defending it, says- If you want to look at any organisation, you should look at it, including its state committee. District presidents are chosen based on the opinion of the people of the district. It is seen who can unite and run the organisation? As per need, reshuffles have been made in many districts from time to time. PDA does not mean that the same equation should be seen everywhere. In the state committee, it is definitely ensured that every section of society gets a place. SP cannot disturb the Yadav-Muslim ratio Senior journalist Brajesh Shukla says - SP's base has always been Yadav-Muslim. In such a situation, no party can move away from its base cadre. It is also natural to see this in SP's organisation. In elections, they certainly give fewer tickets to Yadav-Muslims compared to other castes. This was also seen in the Lok Sabha elections. Even then, SP did not make any Yadav outside the family a candidate. Similarly, they gave fewer tickets to Muslims as well. It has 4 Muslim MPs. However, more tickets were given to non-Yadav OBCs and other castes. There is no guarantee that the PDA slogan, which was popular in the Lok Sabha, will work in 2027. The aggressive stance of the Yadav community in villages is causing resentment among other castes. It may have to pay the price for this in the assembly elections. Dalits appear united with the BSP. Similarly, the BJP is also preparing to give a large number of tickets to the extremely backward classes. In such a situation, it seems difficult for PDA to remain united in favor of the SP.

stories.title: YouTuber Salim Wastik attack case:Victim regains consciousness after 7 days; doctors fear he may lose ability to speak
stories.summary: Salim Wastik, who calls himself an ex-Muslim, regained consciousness 7 days after the attack. Max Hospital administration has given a video to his son, Usman. In this 5-second visual, Salim Vastik is seen on the bed. He has oxygen attached, and stitches are visible on his throat. The doctor says - Salim... He (Salim) opens his eyes and looks. The doctor says - Stick out your tongue... Salim sticks out his tongue. The doctor says - Good. The family has been informed that Salim's condition is much better after the operation, and the medicines are continuously showing effect. On the other hand, the father of Zeeshan and Gulfam from Amroha, who attacked Salim, says - My sons were encountered, and that too was fake. If they made a mistake, they should have been arrested and taken to court. I don't have the means to go to the Supreme Court. Police have not yet been able to clarify who the real mastermind behind the attack on Salim Wastik is? This is why the police are questioning everyone who was in contact with Zeeshan and Gulfam. Now read what Salim's son says about his health... Son said - Dad is reacting, whether he will be able to speak or not, is unknown. Let us tell you that YouTuber Salim Wastik is undergoing treatment at Max Hospital in Delhi. He is currently in the ICU. Salim's son Usman and relatives are present at the hospital. Usman says - Earlier, his father's condition remained serious at GTB Hospital and now at Max Hospital. He was not conscious until now. Today, March 5, he regained consciousness for the first time since the attack on February 27. We are not allowed to go inside. The doctor said that Salim is able to react to sounds but is not yet in a condition to speak. Whether he will be able to speak later or not, the doctor has not clarified yet. Doctors are also saying that the medicines are showing an effect. His condition is continuously improving. Efforts are also underway to recover the liver damage caused by the knife wound with medicines. However, the doctor also said that the wounds are very deep and it may take a long time to fully recover. Wife shifted to a safe place, police van outside the hospital Salim Wastik had kept his wife and son away from himself in Ashok Vihar (Delhi). Where do they live in Ashok Vihar? Police are not disclosing this due to security reasons. The wife has been shifted by the police to a safe place. Son Usman has also been given local police numbers to call for help if he feels any danger. A QRT police van has also been stationed outside Max Hospital in Delhi. Ghaziabad police officers are in contact with the doctors at Max Hospital. Waiting for help for Salim's treatment expenses According to Salim Vastik's family, the entire treatment of Salim Vastik is estimated to cost ₹50 lakh. So far, the expenses have been covered by the savings and the help sent by people. On March 5, Pinky Chaudhary, the national president of Hindu Raksha Dal, also reached Max Hospital. He said, the entire Hindu society stands with Salim. So far, we have provided help worth 4-5 lakh rupees. The entire treatment is expected to cost ₹50 lakh. For security, we are keeping an eye around the hospital. When Salim recovers, we will keep him with us. We will not let him go home. Father's anger in Amroha Said - I am not a beggar, I will earn myself, I will raise my grandson Meanwhile, after the encounter of the two brothers, Zeeshan and Gulfam, in Amroha, their father, Buniyad Ali's anger also came to the fore. He said - If my sons were guilty, they should have been arrested and presented in court. What is this, that they were encountered? That too, fake... We have no demands from our government; we are not beggars. I have two grandsons now, and I will earn in the future, and feed them. Where will I go now? I don't have the means to go to the Supreme Court for justice. He says - Zeeshan was the youngest. He was not married. He was fond of making religious videos and poetry. I am not educated enough to know what is wrong with that. Know Zeeshan and Gulfam, who attacked Salim Gulfam. Zeeshan. Now watch the CCTV footage of the attack on Salim Pakistani YouTuber incited the attack Zeeshan ran a YouTube channel. At the behest of a Pakistani YouTuber, Zeeshan, along with his brother, launched a deadly attack on Salim. Both brothers were connected to a radical organisation's Telegram group. This group has 18,200 members. Admitted on Telegram group - Salim sent to hospital After the attack on Salim, a photo of Salim was posted on the Telegram group with the caption: Salim Ex-Muslim has been sent to the hospital, want video? After this, CM Yogi had given instructions to teach a lesson. The police had announced a reward of ₹1-1 lakh for Zeeshan and Gulfam. Both have been encountered. Came from Amroha on February 17, started keeping an eye on Salim from the 18th In the case of the deadly attack on Salim Wastik, important information has come into the hands of the investigation agencies. Zeeshan and Gulfam had been keeping an eye on Salim's movements for the last 10 days, i.e., since February 18. During this time, he attempted to attack 3 times, but failed every time. Because each time, someone or the other was sitting in his office with Salim. Therefore, he could not attack. On February 27, when Salim returned after offering prayers and was alone in the office, Zeeshan and Gulfam succeeded in their intentions. Met family on 17th, posted video Not only this, Zeeshan knew beforehand what could happen to him after the attack, so he left the village on February 17 after meeting his parents for the last time, and on this day, he made his last video and uploaded it to his Instagram account. In this video, he is seen sitting in an auto, with ghazal lines playing in the background. Keep your passion ready for the journey, be unaware but know everything, who knows when you have to depart, keep your belongings brief. From the next day, i.e., February 18, Zeeshan and Gulfam started keeping an eye on Salim's movements. Gulpham was identified by his round cap ADCP Piyush Kumar Singh said - a .32 bore pistol, 2 cartridges, a KTM bike without a number plate, a mobile phone, an Aadhaar card, a driving license, and a backpack were recovered from Gulpham. He said that Gulpham, wearing a round cap, matched the CCTV footage. A sweater, another round cap, a jacket, and a mobile charger were found in his bag. On February 27, both brothers attacked Salim Wastik with a knife. Salim defended himself with an iron rod. During this, Gulpham's right hand was injured, and Gulpham got treated at a hospital in Gurugram. Stitches were found on his right hand. Police investigation revealed that the bike used at the time of the attack belonged to Zeeshan's maternal uncle, Rashid, which Zeeshan himself used to ride. Read the story of Zeeshan and Gulfam's encounter in 2 points DCP Piyush Singh said- On Sunday night, Loni Police Station in-charge Nitin Chaudhary and the rural SWAT team saw 2 suspects coming on a bike. When they tried to stop them, both fired at the police with pistols. About 25 to 30 rounds of firing took place for about 15 minutes. One bullet hit the criminal. During interrogation, he revealed that he had attacked Salim. His absconding accomplice is his elder brother, Gulfam. The police took the injured Zeeshan to the hospital. There, doctors declared him dead. 48 hours later, information was received that Gulfam was in the Indirapuram police station area. A cordon was set up in front of Vasundhara Power House. At night, a bike was seen approaching. Two people were riding on the bike. When asked to stop, the bike turned to the right. The SWAT team pursued. Due to a mound of earth, the criminals' bike skidded, and they fell. Seeing the police approach, they started firing. In retaliatory firing, a bullet hit Gulfam. Injured Gulfam was sent to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. YouTuber Salim Ahmed alias Salim Wastik (50) lives with his family in Ashok Vihar Colony, Delhi. He has another house in the Loni area of Ghaziabad. Salim runs his office from there. His son Usman said that his father was sitting alone in the office at 9 am on February 27. Then 2 youths wearing helmets came and attacked him. As soon as they entered, they stabbed him repeatedly. Usman said - his father fell to the ground injured. Blood started flowing from his body. Meanwhile, both the assailants fled. Neighbours, hearing the screams, informed the police. Salim was taken to a nearby hospital, from where he was referred to Guru Tegh Bahadur Hospital (GTB) in Delhi. His condition remains serious. Son Usman had filed a complaint with the police. It is named Ashfaq, Sonu, Shahrukh Neta, Bhati Builder, and a local AIMIM leader, Azgar. The FIR mentioned 2 unknown persons. It was alleged that these people had conspired to murder his father Salim.

Straddling Europe and Asia, it borders Russia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, and Iran. stories.title: ‘A strong fist doesn't mean strong reason’: China warns against interference, regime change in Iran
stories.summary: China's foreign minister Wang Yi cautioned against externally driven regime change in Iran, stating such efforts would lack public backing and escalate regional instability. He emphasized respecting Iran's sovereignty and urged an immediate end to hostilities, advocating for diplomatic solutions and independent regional self-determination. Beijing is ready to help restore order and peace.

stories.title: Nitish Kumar's son Nishant enters politics, joins JD(U)
stories.summary: Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar's son, Nishant Kumar, has formally joined the JD(U). This development follows Nitish Kumar's decision to step down as CM, sparking speculation about his successor and potentially ushering in a new political era in Bihar. Nitish Kumar himself announced his intention to contest the Rajya Sabha elections.

stories.title: Over 52,000 Indians fly home from UAE, Gulf within a week as authorities issue update amid US-Iran conflict
stories.summary: Over 52,000 Indian citizens safely returned from the Gulf region between March 1-7, 2026, following recent disruptions. Commercial and rescue flights facilitated the repatriation, with Indian carriers transporting 32,107 passengers. The government remains vigilant, maintaining dedicated helplines for ongoing diaspora welfare.

stories.title: 'Changing face of the Middle East': Netanyahu thanks Trump for strikes on Iran; claims 'control' over Tehran skies
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced near-total dominance over Iranian airspace following coordinated strikes with the US, dubbed 'Operation Rising Lion.' He stated the campaign, supported by former President Trump, aimed to neutralize an immediate threat from Iran's nuclear ambitions and missile program, emphasizing a strategic shift in the region post-October 7th.

stories.title: Top 10 richest people in the world 2026: Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, and other tech titans leading global wealth
Mamata absent, no water in President Murmu's washroom, garbage on road: Centre, Bengal govt spar over 'lapses' at Santal event
stories.summary: The Centre has demanded a response from the West Bengal government by Sunday evening regarding alleged protocol violations during President Droupadi Murmu's visit to state. These alleged lapses include issues with venue arrangements, route cleanliness, and the absence of key state officials at her reception, prompting criticism from the Prime Minister.

stories.title: US embassy in UAE issues security alert: Americans urged to consider leaving as consular services shut
stories.summary: The U.S. Embassy in Abu Dhabi and Consulate General in Dubai issued an urgent security alert for American citizens in the UAE due to escalating regional tensions and potential security risks. Non-emergency government employees and families were ordered to leave the country as a precaution amid ongoing conflict and drone activity.

stories.title: 'Greatest force of change': On Women's Day, Rahul Gandhi shares video of interaction with girl students in Keralam - watch
'Delhi has zero tolerance for heinous criminal, violent incidents': CM Rekha Gupta condemns Uttam Nagar Holi murder, assures strict action
'Mind your own business': Kamal Haasan’s sharp message to Trump on India's oil policy
Dubai travel update: What you need to know as airlines restart operations in phases
Failed Israeli mission to recover pilot’s remains leaves 41 dead in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli special forces operation in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley, targeting Nabi Sheet, aimed to locate the remains of missing airman Ron Arad. The overnight raid, involving air strikes and ground clashes, resulted in 41 deaths and 40 injuries, according to Lebanese health officials. Israel confirmed the operation's failure to find Arad's remains but reiterated its commitment to finding missing servicemen.

stories.title: 'If you kill Americans, we'll kill you': US releases montage of precision strikes with a blunt warning
stories.summary: US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth issued a stark warning of lethal consequences for targeting Americans, amplified by CENTCOM on X. This declaration follows a joint US-Israel strike on Iranian territory that reportedly killed Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, leading to Iranian retaliatory strikes across the region. President Trump claimed significant neutralization of Iranian leadership and military capabilities.

stories.title: Eid Al Fitr 2026 likely to fall on March 20 in UAE, say Sharjah astronomers
Explosives thrown outside New York mayor Zohran Mamdani's residence; 6 arrested
stories.summary: Six individuals were arrested following violent clashes between far-right protesters and counter-protesters outside Gracie Mansion. One protester is accused of throwing smoking projectiles filled with nuts and bolts, prompting an investigation by the FBI and NYPD. The incident began with a demonstration organized by Jake Lang against the city's Muslim mayor.

stories.title: 'Pillars of progressive nation': President Murmu, PM Modi hail 'nari shakti' on International Women's Day
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Droupadi Murmu extended heartfelt greetings on International Women's Day, celebrating 'Nari Shakti's' pivotal role in India's progress. Both leaders lauded women's determination, creativity, and zeal, emphasizing their empowerment as central to national development and the creation of an inclusive, prosperous society where every woman can achieve her full potential.

stories.title: Blast at US embassy in Oslo: Explosion causes minor damage
stories.summary: An explosion struck the consular section entrance of the US Embassy in Oslo early Sunday, with police confirming no injuries were reported. The cause of the blast, which caused minor damage, is under investigation, though authorities believe it may have been an individual act. Investigations are ongoing, with a bomb squad deployed and a large security presence established.

stories.title: Up to Dh200,000 fine, two years in jail: UAE cracks down on spreading rumours during regional crisis
President Murmu unhappy over venue change, PM Modi calls it an 'insult'; Mamata hits back — what triggered Santal conference row
stories.summary: A political storm erupted after West Bengal's last-minute venue change for the International Santhal Conclave, drawing public displeasure from President Murmu. She questioned the reasoning and highlighted the community's struggle for recognition, sparking a fierce exchange between the TMC and BJP over alleged politicization of tribal issues and disrespect to the President's office.

stories.title: 'Not helping them much': Trump downplays reports of Russia sharing intel with Iran
stories.summary: Trump downplayed reports of Russia sharing intelligence with Iran to target US forces, stating it "is not helping them much" given recent events. He suggested that even if such sharing occurred, Iran has gained little, and dismissed concerns about US-Russia relations. Trump also indicated the US would not immediately tap its Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address rising oil prices.

stories.title: Manacles on Jharkhand's trafficked girls — broken by city's rescue facility
Khamenei gone but regime change in Iran 'unlikely', US intelligence warns — report
stories.summary: A joint US-Israeli attack killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, fulfilling President Trump's "regime change" calls. However, a classified intelligence report suggests this is unlikely to topple the entrenched clerical and military establishment, even with a large-scale assault. Analysts concluded Iran's system would likely continue functioning due to established continuity procedures.

stories.title: UAE President's Televised Address: Sheikh Mohamed urges unity after attacks; pledges to defend all
stories.summary: UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan reassured citizens and residents after visiting those injured by regional conflict debris. He pledged the nation's defence and protection for all, emphasising resilience and unity amidst escalating Middle East tensions. The leader urged forgiveness for any shortcomings, highlighting the UAE's strength and commitment to its diverse population.

stories.title: China tells at-risk people to undergo cancer screening
stories.summary: China's health ministry is urging individuals aged 50 and above, smokers, and those with a family history of lung cancer to get annual low-dose CT scans. This initiative is part of a national campaign to significantly enhance cancer prevention and control efforts by the year 2030, aiming for broader public health improvements.

stories.title: Gulf crisis: Now, Kuwait announces cuts in oil, refining output
stories.summary: Kuwait, a major OPEC member, has significantly reduced its oil and refinery output due to threats against shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Citing "ongoing aggression by the Islamic Republic of Iran," the nation began cutting production by 100,000 barrels daily, with further substantial reductions planned. These measures highlight escalating regional tensions impacting global energy supplies.

stories.title: Iran ‘struck’ high-value US radar systems in Gulf, show satellite images
stories.summary: Iran has reportedly targeted key US radar and early warning systems across the Gulf, including advanced THAAD missile defense components in Jordan and Qatar, and a satellite communications hub in the UAE. These strikes, if confirmed, could significantly degrade American military surveillance and missile defense capabilities in West Asia, with substantial financial losses for the US.

stories.title: China asserts need for more power as Donald Trump embraces war
stories.summary: Chinese analysts believe the US would not target Xi Jinping like it did Khamenei due to China's nuclear status. However, Trump's embrace of war reinforces Beijing's view of the US as its primary threat, prompting calls for superior firepower and self-reliance. China also warns against internal threats and deceptive negotiations with Washington.

stories.title: UAE: Dubai confirms driver killed after debris from intercepted missile strikes car in Al Barsha amid Iran vs US-Israel war
stories.summary: A Pakistani driver tragically died in Dubai when debris from an aerial interception fell on his vehicle. This incident, linked to escalating regional conflict, highlights the unpredictable dangers of modern warfare even with successful air defence. The UAE's advanced systems intercepted threats but falling fragments posed a risk to civilians in densely populated areas.

stories.title: How Army trailblazers inspired generations of women officers
stories.summary: Two women, Lt Col Randhawa (retd) and Major Jhingan (retd), shattered military barriers. Randhawa became India's first war widow officer after her husband's sacrifice, while Jhingan was Lady Cadet 001, paving the way for women in the armed forces. Their journeys inspire countless others to serve the nation.

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh: 2.4 crore names dropped in poll rolls since SIR announced
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh's voter count is approaching 13 crore. A voter roll revision exercise is nearing completion. Notices were issued and hearings held for millions of voters. Many names were removed due to migration or other reasons. Thousands of applications for corrections and updates were also processed. The final electoral roll will be published soon.

stories.title: Peaceful Nepal elections historic, ready to work with new government: PM Modi
stories.summary: Nepal's elections saw a landslide victory for Balendra Shah's Rastriya Swatantra Party. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Nepal on its peaceful polls, highlighting the vibrant exercise of democratic rights. Shah, a rapper-turned-politician, projects a 'Nepal First' hyper-nationalism, emphasizing neutrality in foreign policy.

stories.title: Government to hire 1,000 professionals to help exporters
stories.summary: The government is set to recruit 1,000 young professionals to boost India's export potential. These individuals will work with businesses nationwide, encouraging greater use of Free Trade Agreement (FTA) benefits and aiding in product and market diversification. This initiative aims to invigorate manufacturing by promoting goods moving overseas through preferential duties, especially for FTAs with lower utilization rates.

stories.title: PMO seeks third-party audits for road, rail projects
stories.summary: The PMO is pushing for independent third-party audits in road and rail projects to boost quality and speed up execution. Ministries are tasked with studying past successful construction practices, like those from the Golden Quadrilateral era, and international models from Indonesia and Malaysia.

stories.title: Explosion scare in Dubai Marina: UAE emirate confirms tower hit by falling debris from aerial interception amid Iran and US-Israel clashes
stories.summary: Dubai authorities confirmed that debris from a successful aerial interception, not a direct attack, caused a minor incident in Dubai Marina. The event was linked to regional tensions and ongoing conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel and resulted in falling debris that struck a tower, with no injuries reported.

stories.title: 'Census-style' 45-day assessment signals early learning turnaround in Haryana schools
stories.summary: Haryana's government schools have achieved a remarkable turnaround in foundational learning, with high-performing schools surging from 7% to 53% in just three months. A statewide diagnostic assessment and targeted 45-day remediation drive, focusing on literacy and numeracy, significantly boosted student competencies across nearly 8,600 primary schools.

stories.title: Top legal experts split on social media ban for kids
stories.summary: Legal experts question the effectiveness of state-level bans on social media for children, citing central government jurisdiction over IT and telecommunications. While appreciating the intent to protect young minds, they advocate for education on constructive usage and pan-India legislation rather than fragmented state laws.

stories.title: Seismic map rollback hits quake readiness: Experts
stories.summary: India's decision to withdraw its updated seismic zonation map and earthquake design code has alarmed experts, who fear it weakens national preparedness for major seismic events. The revised framework, which placed the entire Himalayan arc in the highest risk zone, was seen as a crucial step in enhancing disaster resilience and ensuring safer construction practices against devastating earthquakes.

stories.title: Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim acquitted in journalist murder case
stories.summary: Punjab and Haryana High Court acquitted Dera Sacha Sauda chief Gurmeet Ram Rahim in the 2002 murder of journalist Ram Chander Chhatrapati, overturning a life sentence. Ram Rahim remains jailed for rape convictions, and his family plans to challenge the acquittal in the Supreme Court.

stories.title: Congress: US calling India 'good actor' is evidence of PM Modi's cowardice
stories.summary: Congress criticizes the Modi government, calling Prime Minister Modi's actions "cowardly" after the US Treasury Secretary praised India for agreeing to halt Russian oil imports. The party also attacked the government over rising LPG prices, highlighting a contradiction with the Petroleum Minister's earlier statement on affordable fuel.

stories.title: Government takes steps to train 85,000 chip designers in 315 institutions
stories.summary: India's Chips to Startups programme is training engineers in semiconductor design. Students from 315 institutions are gaining hands-on experience. The government plans to expand this initiative to 500 institutions. This aims to build a strong talent pipeline for the growing global semiconductor industry. The programme is part of India's larger semiconductor mission.

stories.title: Stress, panic or burnout? Free mental health helplines that are open 24/7 in the UAE
stories.summary: Mental health awareness is growing across the UAE. Free and confidential helplines are now available 24 hours a day. These services offer immediate support for anxiety, stress and other emotional challenges. Organizations like SAKINA and the National Mental Support Line provide crucial assistance. This initiative ensures accessible help for everyone, promoting wellbeing nationwide.

stories.title: LPG price hike: Mamata calls for protests, Sidda seeks PM Modi's ouster
stories.summary: Opposition-ruled states are fiercely criticizing the central government over surging LPG prices. West Bengal's Chief Minister urged women to protest on Women's Day against the hike and voter list deletions. Karnataka's CM blamed PM Modi's foreign policy for the price rise, demanding his resignation. Jharkhand's JMM spokesperson pointed to strained ties with Russia as a contributing factor.

stories.title: TMC government has crossed all limits, says PM Modi over President Murmu's venue, protocol plaint
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticized the West Bengal government for disrespecting constitutional office and tribal communities after President Droupadi Murmu expressed disappointment over her reception and event organization. Modi called the incident shameful and unprecedented, highlighting the insult to the President and the casual treatment of Santal culture. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP of political maneuvering.

stories.title: Doctors warn against frequent use of morning-after pills
stories.summary: Women relying on morning-after pills face health risks, doctors warn. Frequent use disrupts hormonal balance and menstrual cycles, with potential long-term reproductive health impacts. These pills are for emergencies, not routine contraception, and do not protect against STIs. Experts urge considering more reliable birth control methods if frequent use is needed.

stories.title: LPG price hike: Domestic cooking gas cost up by Rs 60 a cylinder
stories.summary: Domestic LPG cylinders will now cost Rs 60 more, reaching Rs 913 in Delhi, while commercial prices saw a Rs 114.5 increase. This hike, attributed to global energy market pressures and the West Asia conflict, comes despite government efforts to shield households. Ujjwala beneficiaries will pay Rs 613, with a Rs 300 subsidy.

stories.title: EAM Jaishankar: Let Iranian ship dock on humanitarian grounds
stories.summary: India's ascent is unstoppable, driven by its own strength, not others' missteps, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar asserted. He confirmed India granted humanitarian docking to Iranian ship IRIS LAVAN in Kochi following technical issues, days before another Iranian warship was sunk. Jaishankar emphasized India's role as a security provider in the Indian Ocean, guided by humanitarian principles.

stories.title: Congress sees notice against Om Birla as 'strong message'
stories.summary: Congress believes the removal notice against Speaker Om Birla sends a strong message about the undermining of the opposition under BJP rule. The opposition is buoyed by TMC's support for the no-confidence motion, aiming to show a vertically divided Lok Sabha and highlight an unequal parliamentary battle.

stories.title: Punjab: Police officer beaten to death in village near Amritsar
stories.summary: An Assistant Sub-Inspector, Jagjit Singh, was tragically beaten to death in his native village near Amritsar following a personal dispute. The altercation reportedly began when relatives of his son's girlfriend raised objections, escalating into a violent scuffle where the ASI was struck with iron rods. Five suspects have been apprehended, with police continuing efforts to locate others involved.

stories.title: Government may scrap NOC for inter-state vehicle transfers
stories.summary: Inter-state vehicle transfers are set to become significantly easier as the government plans to eliminate the need for No Objection Certificates (NOCs). A NITI Aayog committee recommended an auto-generated clearance system, leveraging the centralized VAHAN database. This reform will greatly benefit vehicle owners relocating between states, streamlining the registration process.

stories.title: Emaar founder boldly reveals why Dubai’s property market has ‘nothing to fear’ amid Iran and US-Israel war
stories.summary: Despite regional geopolitical tensions and an anticipated surge in new housing supply, Dubai's real estate sector remains resilient, according to Emaar Properties founder Mohamed Alabbar. He asserts that the market has strong fundamentals and long-term planning to weather shocks, with record sales and luxury segment growth fueling optimism for continued stability and expansion.

stories.title: Gulf conflict: Indians in Bahrain, Qatar eye Saudi visas to fly out
stories.summary: Indians in Qatar and Bahrain are seeking Saudi transit visas as a backup plan due to flight cancellations. With airports in Doha and Bahrain largely shut, many are preparing for overland journeys to Saudi Arabia or Oman. This comes amid ongoing regional tensions, prompting a need for alternative travel routes home.

stories.title: UAE Lottery: Over 8,000 residents bag prizes while Dh30 million jackpot still waiting
stories.summary: The UAE Lottery's "Lucky Day" draw saw over 8,299 winners, with four individuals securing Dh100,000 each. Despite the substantial number of winners, the Dh30 million jackpot remained unclaimed, continuing the excitement for a life-changing win. The lottery has already distributed over Dh147 million to more than 100,000 players since its launch.

stories.title: ‘I like Kamla better’: Trump jokes about similarity between Trinidad PM’s name and Kamala Harris — watch
stories.summary: During the 2026 Summit of the Americas, President Trump lightheartedly noted the similarity between Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar's first name and former Vice President Kamala Harris. Trump joked about the pronunciation difference, stating he preferred 'Kamla' and humorously warned against mixing them up. The exchange occurred as leaders gathered to discuss regional security and migration.

stories.title: Southwest flight diverted mid-air over 'possible security matter'; FBI confirms no threat
Zohran Mamdani reassured Jewish New Yorkers but his wife’s Oct 7 social media activity tells another story
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani faces questions regarding his administration's stance against antisemitism. This follows resurfaced social media activity by his wife, Rama Duwaji, liking posts after the October 7 Hamas attack. Mamdani's past support for pro-Palestinian movements and criticism of Israel also draw attention. The controversy highlights concerns within the city's large Jewish community.

stories.title: 'He handles unruly MPs from big families well': PM Modi lauds Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi lauded Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla ahead of an opposition no-confidence motion, praising his impartiality and ability to manage "arrogant and unruly" members. Birla's recent rulings, particularly disallowing a quote from a former Army chief, had sparked significant opposition protests and led to the removal notice.

stories.title: 'What is with this obsession with Indians?': Indian Entrepreneur hits out at criticism of folk dancer
stories.summary: An Indian entrepreneur in Germany labeled backlash against a folk dancer at the Washington Monument as "straight up racism," highlighting perceived double standards. He questioned the intense negativity towards Indian immigrants and their cultural expressions, suggesting appreciation and gratitude would be more fitting responses.

stories.title: US student visas for Indians fall 61% last year, only 22,000 issued, colleges sound alarm
Jammu and Kashmir: 2 mobiles, being smuggled inside jail, recovered in Doda
stories.summary: Authorities at Bhaderwah Jail in Doda district intercepted two mobile phones hidden within a parcel intended for an inmate held under the Public Safety Act. The parcel, addressed to Irshad Ahmad Wani, a resident of Bandipora, was reportedly booked by Mohammed Younis Wani from Pulwama.

stories.title: Jammu: NIA court rejects bail plea of terror funding accused
stories.summary: A Jammu NIA court denied bail to Tanvir Ahmed Wani, accused in a terror funding case. Wani allegedly conspired with Pakistani traders, importing goods beyond limits via under-invoicing to generate profits for terror outfits like Hizbul Mujahideen and Lashkar-e-Taiba. Incriminating materials were found at his residence.

stories.title: Visually impaired Kashmir youth cracks civil services, daily-wager father recounts years of struggle
stories.summary: In Bandipora, Kashmir, Irfan Ahmad Lone, a visually impaired youth, has achieved a remarkable feat by clearing the UPSC civil services exams with a rank of 957. Despite facing severe vision loss in childhood due to accidents, Irfan pursued his education with unwavering determination, graduating from JNU and working before his civil services success.

stories.title: Inside world’s longest non-stop flight set to launch next year, where passengers see two sunrises
stories.summary: Qantas is set to launch its Project Sunrise flights, linking Sydney non-stop to London and New York, over 10,000 miles in around 22 hours. Using specially configured Airbus A350-1000ULR aircraft, the airline aims to cut travel time, reduce jet lag, and offer wellness-focused cabins. The ambitious ultra-long-haul service could transform global aviation and redefine long-distance travel experiences.

stories.title: UAE residents turn to secret land routes to escape travel shutdown amid Iran and US–Israel war
stories.summary: Escalating Iran-US-Israel conflict has caused unprecedented travel disruptions across the Middle East. Thousands of travelers and expatriates in the Gulf are now using land corridors and emergency services to leave the region as airspace closures and flight cancellations persist. This crisis is reshaping regional mobility and impacting global aviation networks.

stories.title: Indian-origin British surgeon performs UK’s first long-distance operation from 2,400 km away using robotic equipment
'Blaming H-1Bs when...': Hindu American group slams Texas politicians for linking Austin shooting to immigrants
Students showcase STEM projects at science carnival in Navi Mumbai
stories.summary: The seventh Amazon Think Big Science Carnival in Navi Mumbai showcased student innovations addressing real-world challenges. Over 12,000 students participated, with 20 teams presenting working prototypes on themes like "STEM for Sustainability" and "Tech for Good." The event fostered analytical thinking and teamwork through interactive exhibits and competitions.

stories.title: ‘Take this down’: Man attacked after tearing down Khamenei’s poster at NYC vigil; multiple detained —
Delhi CM hops on DTC bus to check implementation of Saheli Pink Smart Card
Jeffrey Epstein guard googled him 40 minutes before his death and made $5K cash deposit days earlier: DoJ files show
stories.summary: New Justice Department documents reveal Tova Noel, Epstein's guard, Googled him minutes before his death and made a large cash deposit prior. She allegedly falsified records, admitting to not always performing required checks. The FBI identified her as a possible orange figure near his cell on surveillance footage, a detail previously unconfirmed.

stories.title: Dubai: British trainer Antonia Bettridge, 25, faces life in prison, ‘devastated’ mum speaks out
stories.summary: British personal trainer Antonia Bettridge, 25, from St Helens, faces possible life imprisonment in Dubai after being detained on suspicion of possessing narcotics with intent to distribute. Her family, speaking through Detained in Dubai, says they are desperate for clarity while UK officials confirm they are providing consular support.

stories.title: Uttarakhand: Amit Shah inaugurates 'Nootan Nyaya Sanhita' exhibition in Haridwar
stories.summary: The exhibition aims to spread awareness and highlight the effective implementation of the new criminal laws introduced by the Government of India, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA).

stories.title: Amit Shah recalls Uttarakhand statehood movement during 'Jan Jan Ki Sarkar, 4 Saal Bemisaal' in Hardwar
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday recalled the Uttarakhand statehood movement, saying that the youth of Uttarakhand had to take to the streets to protect their identity, culture, and rights. During this struggle, they also had to face incidents of violence such as the Rampur Tiraha firing incident.

stories.title: Who is Estefany Rodriguez Flores? Nashville reporter arrested by ICE after living lawfully in US for five years
stories.summary: Reporter Estefany Rodriguez Flores was arrested by ICE in Nashville during a traffic stop, with her lawyers claiming no warrant was present. ICE stated she violated her visa terms and has no lawful status, detaining her pending immigration proceedings. Her colleagues and supporters are advocating for her release, citing her legal entry and asylum application.

stories.title: Misreading Iran? A week into war, strategic risks for Trump and US are growing
stories.summary: A week into the US-Israeli war against Iran, President Trump faces escalating military, economic, and political risks as the conflict widens regionally. Despite early battlefield gains and the killing of Iran's supreme leader, the operation's unclear endgame and potential for prolonged engagement raise concerns about global stability and domestic political fallout.

stories.title: Random Musing: Donald Trump has only one red line. Kristi Noem crossed it...
stories.summary: Franz Kafka wrote in the Zürau Aphorisms: “There are two cardinal sins from which all others spring: impatience and laziness. Because of impatience we were driven out of Paradise, because of laziness we cannot return.” In Trumpian paradise, there are also two original sins: blaming Trump for something and being caught on camera blaming Trump for something.

stories.title: Murmu-Mamata row escalates: PM Modi says 'TMC govt crossed all limits'; Bengal CM advises President 'don't indulge in politics'
Abdullah Alwan, Mughith Faisal and Basheer Faisal: Three men sentenced in Phoenix for defrauding Amazon of millions of dollars
From SHGs to drone technology: Inside India’s growing push for women’s economic empowerment
stories.summary: India is championing women's financial empowerment, with initiatives like Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana and the NaMo Drone Didi program enabling women to build independent livelihoods. Self-help groups are thriving, offering credit and skills, while entrepreneurship schemes and financial inclusion policies are bringing more women into the economic mainstream, fostering inclusive national development.

stories.title: 'Pause all immigration': US Rep Chip Roy asked to stop until 'broken H-1B system revamped'
stories.summary: US Representative Chip Roy is urging a halt to all immigration, advocating for a pause until the H-1B visa system and the broader immigration framework are thoroughly reformed. He emphasized the need to address visa overstays and ensure national security before resuming immigration, highlighting concerns about the current system's vulnerabilities and potential exploitation.

stories.title: The girl in the frame and an aunt in the shadows: Could North Korea get its first female supreme leader?
‘Xi’s world order died with Khamenei’: The good, the bad, and ugly of US-Iran war for China
stories.summary: China's strategy of balancing interests in the Middle East is challenged by US actions against Iran. This conflict reveals Beijing's inability to protect its partners and reinforces President Xi Jinping's focus on military strength. The situation impacts China's energy security and global standing. Upcoming talks with President Trump will occur amidst these strategic shifts.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi says PM Modi 'betrayed the country' by signing US trade deal
stories.summary: Rahul said the entry of large and mechanised American agricultural corporations into the Indian market would put small farmers under severe pressure and could lead to "devastation" in the agricultural sector. He further alleged that the country’s energy sector had been compromised and claimed that US President Donald Trump had obtained Indian data through the agreement.

stories.title: Gold, cash & more! TVK chief Vijay wooes women voters, promises 'super-good regime'
‘Stop Indian Hate’: Indian American group launches tracker to document rising anti-Indian hate in US
‘My wife is a private person’: Zohran Mamdani responds to report on her October 7 social media likes
stories.summary: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani addressed reports of his wife liking social media content celebrating the October 7 attacks. While acknowledging his wife's private status, Mamdani asserted his responsibility to answer for his own actions and policies as an elected official representing all New Yorkers. He reiterated his condemnation of the Hamas attack.

stories.title: Indian national Jashanpreet Singh arrested by ICE in San Diego over alleged criminal history, may face deportation
Evening news wrap: EAM reacts to Iranian ship sinking in Indian Ocean; why US 'agreed to let' India buy Russian oil & more
'I'm very sad': President Murmu objects to Mamata govt allotting smaller venue for Santhal event
stories.summary: The President said she was very sad about the last minute change in the venue and also pointed out how chief minister Mamata Banerjee chose not to meet her, which is against the set norm. Murmu on Saturday said the contributions of the Santals to the country's freedom struggle have not received due recognition, and asserted that the names of several legends belonging to the community were "not deliberately included in history".

stories.title: 'Reflects friendly ties': Iran thanks India for letting IRIS Lavan dock in Kochi
Qatar announces Ramadan I’tikaf rules: New age limits and mosque guidelines worshippers should know
stories.summary: Qatar has introduced new guidelines for its traditional Ramadan mosque retreat, I'tikaf. The rules, aimed at maintaining order and hygiene, clarify age restrictions and specify that participation is currently limited to men. These measures ensure worshippers can focus on prayer and spiritual reflection during the holy month's final, significant days.

stories.title: Planning to get Botox or fillers? Saudi Arabia tightens rules, mandates specialist supervision
From Tamil Nadu to West Bengal: How governor RN Ravi’s transfer impacts two poll-bound states
Middle East crisis: Are Iran's ballistic missiles running out amid US-Israel strikes?
stories.summary: Iran's missile attacks have dropped significantly. US and Israeli strikes have destroyed many launchers, crippling Iran's ability to launch missiles. Stockpiles are also depleted. Iran is now shifting to drones and proxy groups for attacks. This strategy change is forcing Tehran to rely on other means to pressure adversaries in the region and beyond.

stories.title: Uttarakhand ranks first in country in effective implementation of new criminal laws
stories.summary: Uttarakhand has secured the first position in the national implementation of the Inter-Operable Criminal Justice System (ICJS) 2.0, according to data up to January 2026.

stories.title: 52,360 people flown from Gulf to India till Friday midnight on 280 flights: DGCA
IndiGo extends free cancellation waiver for Middle East flights amid regional crisis
Planning to go out in Dubai this weekend? Check which attractions are closed
When cost stops being the barrier: The new chapter of Ozempic injection in India
stories.summary: The upcoming patent expiry for Ozempic in India is set to dramatically lower the cost of semaglutide, making this once-premium diabetes and weight-loss drug accessible to more patients. This shift could reshape the market, prompting earlier prescriptions and potentially altering societal views on weight management and body acceptance.

stories.title: LuLu Group airlifts 80,000kg of Indian produce to UAE to keep supermarket shelves stocked
stories.summary: Dedicated cargo flights are delivering fresh produce to the UAE as regional aviation disruptions impact traditional supply routes. Retailers are arranging special shipments from overseas to ensure supermarket shelves remain stocked with fruits, vegetables, and other perishables, maintaining steady supplies for residents.

stories.summary: UAE air travel is slowly resuming with limited flights on March 7 after regional airspace closures. Strict airport entry protocols are in place, with travelers urged to confirm flight status before departure due to rapidly changing schedules.

No confidence motion against Om Birla: TMC MPs likely to vote in favour of resolution

stories.summary: Global oil prices have surged dramatically this week. The ongoing conflict involving Iran has intensified, raising fears of prolonged energy supply disruptions from the Middle East. stories.title: Pakistan's Asim Munir meets Saudi defence minister: Is 'Islamic Nato' in play?
stories.summary: Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir met Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman amidst escalating Middle East tensions following Iranian attacks. This move aims to digitize patient records, enabling verification of Ayushman Bharat beneficiaries and weeding out fake entries. It will also allow doctors to access patient medical histories for seamless treatment and improve regulatory oversight of teaching hospitals.

NH users who fail to pay toll to get 3 days to make payment

stories.summary: Israeli forces launched broad-scale strikes on targets in Tehran, including Mehrabad International Airport, with explosions reported across the city and surrounding areas. stories.title: Iran delays naming supreme leader out of security concerns: Officials
stories.summary: Iran has delayed naming a successor to its supreme leader due to security concerns, following threats from the US and Israel against potential candidates. Ayatollah Khamenei's son, Mojtaba, is a leading contender, but American and Israeli officials have publicly stated he would be an "unacceptable" target for elimination.

stories.title: Emirates NBD bank waives ATM fees across UAE, GCC as war fears grow
stories.summary: Emirates NBD is waiving ATM withdrawal fees across the UAE and GCC until March 31, 2026, to ease financial access amid regional disruptions. This move also includes free debit card replacements and delivery, offering crucial support to stranded travelers and residents navigating travel uncertainties. The initiative aims to ensure uninterrupted access to funds during a turbulent period.

stories.title: US DoJ releases missing interviews with woman who made claims against Donald Trump
stories.summary: The Justice Department has released previously withheld FBI interview notes concerning a woman's accusations of sexual assault against President Trump and Jeffrey Epstein. stories.title: US-Israel-Iran War Live Updates: 'They got caught on wrong side of events': Jaishankar on Iran ship struck by US in Indian Ocean
Middle East tensions: Consider charges waiver for stranded ships, ports told
stories.summary: Indian ports are offering relief to cargo ships stranded due to West Asian conflict. The Shipping Ministry has directed major ports to consider reducing or waiving charges like storage rent and reefer plugging. Ports will also facilitate transshipment, domestic return of export cargo, and priority handling for perishables, aiming to prevent congestion and container shortages.

stories.title: 'Equal work, equal pay' applies only within same institution: Madras high court
stories.summary: The Madras High Court ruled that the principle of equal pay for equal work applies only to employees within the same institution and under identical service conditions. The court clarified that comparisons cannot be made between employees of public sector undertakings and government departments due to differing service rules.

stories.title: PM Modi: Make our agriculture export-oriented
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged farmers to make Indian agriculture export-oriented by leveraging the country's diverse climate to boost productivity and farm produce exports. He highlighted the growing global demand for natural and chemical-free products, suggesting this could open up world markets. The government is considering certification and laboratory support for these initiatives.

stories.title: Middle East tensions: 13 flights bring stranded flyers from Gulf to Mumbai
stories.summary: Mumbai airport received 13 repatriation flights from Fujairah and Dubai on Friday, bringing home Indian travellers. Despite these arrivals, flight disruptions persisted with 73 air traffic movements cancelled. Appeals for urgent support for Indians stranded in the West Asia war situation continue, with families expressing deep worry.

stories.title: CDC level-2 polio travel advisory: Precautions for international travellers
stories.summary: Global health alerts are up for polio. The CDC warns travellers to take extra care. Poliovirus is detected in many countries. This reminds everyone the fight is not over. Pharmacists play a key role in educating travellers. They check vaccination status and advise on boosters. Staying protected is vital before international travel.

stories.title: In a 1st in India, Karnataka links liquor tax to alcohol content
stories.summary: Karnataka is introducing a new alcohol-in-beverage (AIB) based excise duty system from April, becoming the first state to directly link liquor taxation to alcohol content. This reform aims to modernize the system, improve transparency, and simplify pricing, potentially making beer and wine cheaper. The state also plans to promote alcohol tourism and allow 24-hour operations for distilleries and breweries.

stories.title: ED seizes Rs 441 crore assets in Andhra Pradesh liquor scam case
stories.summary: The Enforcement Directorate has attached properties worth Rs 441 crore in the Andhra Pradesh liquor scam. The probe, based on an AP CID FIR, uncovered a multi-crore fraud involving manipulation of liquor procurement and distribution, allegedly causing a Rs 3,500 crore loss to the state exchequer. The ED has traced a money trail of Rs 1,048 crore in kickbacks.

stories.title: Global conflicts show wars won’t be short, need to build resilient defence industrial capacities: Navy chief
stories.summary: Navy Chief Admiral Dinesh Kumar Tripathi emphasized the critical need for robust industrial preparedness in modern warfare, citing recent global conflicts that have shattered assumptions of short, decisive wars. He highlighted the imperative for nations to cultivate resilient defense industrial capacities, stressing the importance of large-scale production, continuous technological upgrades, and sufficient surge capacity to meet evolving security challenges.

stories.title: Goa cashew fest to create awareness about safe driving
stories.summary: Goa Cashew Fest 2026, from April 10-12 in Panaji, will highlight feni and cashew products while championing safe driving awareness. stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that left-wing extremism will be completely wiped out by March 31, ending the ambition of a "red corridor" from Tirupati to Pashupati. stories.title: Qatar reopens airspace: Allows limited flights as missile strikes continue across Gulf
stories.summary: Qatar has partially reopened its airspace after days of disruption due to regional military tensions. While some evacuation and cargo flights are resuming under strict monitoring, commercial services remain heavily restricted. This move offers a glimmer of hope for stranded travellers and airlines navigating ongoing security concerns across the Middle East.

stories.title: Bihar: Nitish Kumar firm on Rajya Sabha move, son Nishant to join JDU tomorrow
stories.summary: Nishant Kumar, son of Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, is set to join the JDU on March 8, marking his political debut. Nitish Kumar has affirmed his decision to move to the Rajya Sabha is final and irreversible, assuring party members he will remain involved in Bihar's development. stories.title: Daylight saving time 2026: When does DST start in US and Canada? Date, time, why it matters and does it affect your health
stories.summary: America braces for Daylight Saving Time 2026 on March 8, shifting clocks forward and sparking renewed debate. While offering longer evenings, the biannual change disrupts sleep, raising health concerns like increased heart attacks and accidents. Economists also point to potential financial costs, fuelling a growing movement to end the practice.

stories.title: West Bengal: Didi begins sit-in, alleges EC 'plot' to delete voters' names
stories.summary: West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee launched a sit-in protest, accusing the BJP and Election Commission of a conspiracy to disenfranchise voters by removing genuine names from electoral rolls. stories.title: Karnataka says it will ban social media for children under 16
stories.summary: Karnataka plans to ban social media for children under 16, aligning with global efforts to curb digital exposure. Chief Minister Siddaramaiah announced the policy, aiming to address concerns over screen addiction and mental health. While welcomed by educators, experts caution about potential FOMO and withdrawal, urging careful implementation and support for children.

stories.title: Before Dena, India let another Iran ship with 183 crew dock in Kochi
stories.summary: Days before the sinking of IRIS Dena, India granted permission for the Iranian ship IRIS Lavan to dock at Kochi port due to technical issues. This decision, made on March 1, allowed IRIS Lavan and its 183 crew members to safely shelter, avoiding the fate of IRIS Dena which was sunk by a US submarine.

stories.title: US waiver row: BJP flags UPA-era cuts in Iranian crude imports
stories.summary: The BJP highlighted a substantial decrease in India's crude oil imports from Iran during the UPA era, which secured the nation an exemption from US sanctions.
